item.title: Iran's Pezeshkian blames US for interim deal failure, urges new try
item.description: Iranian President Massoud Pezeshkian, in remarks broadcast on state TV on Saturday, blamed the United States for the failure of an interim deal with Iran, but said there should be a new attempt at concluding it.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Iranian President Massoud Pezeshkian, in remarks broadcast on state TV on Saturday, blamed the United States for the failure of an [USN:S8N42O01Z TEXT:"interim deal"] with Iran, but said there should be a new attempt at concluding it. "We were having negotiations, the cowards (Americans) messed everything up...I still think we ahould go and conclude it," Pezeshkian said.

item.title: La Mona Lisa queda fuera del alcance del público tras cierre de museos París por temor a las protestas
item.description: Los decepcionados turistas asomaban la cabeza el sábado por las puertas cerradas del Louvre y se lamentaban que no podrían ver a la Mona Lisa, en una jornada en que las galerías y los museos de todo París cerraron como medida de precaución ante las nuevas manifestaciones.
item.dc:creator: Sybille de La Hamaide
item.content:encoded: Los decepcionados turistas asomaban la cabeza el sábado por las puertas cerradas del Louvre y se lamentaban que no podrían ver a la Mona Lisa, en una jornada en que las galerías y los museos de todo París cerraron como medida de precaución ante las nuevas manifestaciones. "Cuando llegamos, pensamos que podría haber algún problema, pero no que el museo estuviera cerrado", dijo la italiana Selena Bertoni, de 31 años, frente al Museo de Orsay. Los cierres se produjeron una semana después de que las manifestaciones a nivel nacional por el costo de vida y el deterioro de los servicios públicos degeneraran en algunos de los peores episodios de violencia callejera que ha vivido Francia en años. La violencia y los daños llevaron al Gobierno a imponer toques de queda localizados y a cerrar muchos lugares públicos antes de las manifestaciones previstas para el sábado. El cierre se extendió a gran parte del sector cultural de la capital, incluidos los museos de la Orangerie, el Jeu de Paume y el Picasso, mientras que todo el complejo de los Jardines de las Tullerías, que da al Louvre, quedó acordonado. "Este es el tercer museo al que llegamos y que está cerrado. Deberían habernos avisado", comentó la francesa Heidi Rosar, de 21 años. En el Louvre, las puertas de hierro negro cerradas con llave bloqueaban el acceso a todo el recinto y al jardín. "Queríamos ver al menos la pirámide", comentó Don Nowschuk, un canadiense de 67 años, refiriéndose a la emblemática entrada acristalada del museo. Nowschuk sugirió que las autoridades locales podrían estar exagerando. "Hay tanta seguridad que uno pensaría que sería suficiente para proteger el museo (...) Es un poco extraño ver tantos policías armados por todo París. Estamos acostumbrados a las armas, pero no así". Las restricciones se extendieron al sector de las artes escénicas. La Ópera de París cerró tanto el Palais Garnier como la Ópera de la Bastilla, alegando motivos de seguridad para el personal y el público.

item.title: Trump says he may move White House press corps
item.description: US President Donald Trump confirmed on Saturday he may move the White House press corps to a different location.
item.dc:creator: Jason Lange
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump confirmed on Saturday he may move the White House press corps to a different location. In a social media post, Trump dismissed a report that he planned to remove the White House press room and restore a historic swimming pool on the site, saying he had never "even thought to do such a stupid thing." But he said he could relocate the press corps from its current position in the White House. "I may move the Fake News to a less obnoxious location," Trump said in the post. The New York Times reported on Tuesday that Trump had urged then-press secretary Karoline Leavitt in August to move news conferences out of the White House's James S. Brady Press Briefing Room, although the idea was never implemented. According to the report, the president told aides he would rather have an indoor therapy pool that was installed at the site during Franklin D. Roosevelt's administration. The Nixon administration replaced the pool with the press briefing room. Trump has regularly accused US media of unfair reporting about his administration. Last month, Trump briefly banned journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico from White House grounds and said other outlets could face similar restrictions. Free speech advocates have said the move violated First Amendment protections for a free press. The White House reinstated their access after an order from a federal judge who deemed the ban likely unconstitutional, although the Trump administration is still contesting the case.

item.title: Lightning, Mammoth enjoying strong starts to season
item.description: Through a combined 21 games played, the Tampa Bay Lightning and Utah Mammoth are trending in the right direction: upward in their respective divisions.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Through a combined 21 games played, the Tampa Bay Lightning and Utah Mammoth are trending in the right direction: upward in their respective divisions. The two clubs will meet Saturday night in Salt Lake City in the first of two games against each other this season. Entering the Saturday clash, the Mammoth are atop the Central Division, tied with Minnesota with 14 points through 11 games apiece. After Saturday, the Wild will be the next opponent for the Mammoth -- Tuesday in Salt Lake City. Utah is coming off of a 5-3 setback on Thursday against the Kraken in Seattle. The Mammoth got two goals from Logan Cooley and one tally from Vincent Trocheck, as each forward netted on the power play. The Mammoth went 2-for-3 on the man advantage and outshot the Kraken 36-23. Skating with the Florida Panthers, Carolina Hurricanes and New York Rangers for 13 seasons, the 33-year-old Trocheck was acquired from the Rangers over the summer for Sean Durzi, Cole Beaudoin and a 2027 third-round draft pick. "I think the comfortability with each other and getting back into the rhythm of playing the right way has gotten better each game," said the Pittsburgh native, who has three goals, two assists and is 61.4% on faceoffs. "I think how fast we are and how fast we play is tough to play against, especially when teams aren't able to change (lines)." Stopping pucks has been an issue for Utah goaltenders Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa. Vejmelka is the team's No. 1 goalie with a 5-3-0 mark and a 3.04 goals-against average and an .874 save percentage. The 6-foot-6 Cossa is 2-1-0 with a 3.33 GAA and an .820 save rate. Tampa Bay, which is tied for second place in the Atlantic Division, will conclude a three-game road trip on Saturday after a win against the Vegas Golden Knights and a loss to the Colorado Avalanche. A perennial powerhouse, Colorado entered the game three points behind the Mammoth in the Central. However, the Avalanche crafted an early 3-0 lead, received a four-point night from Nathan MacKinnon, and won 6-3 despite Jake Guentzel scoring twice for the Lightning as their three-game winning streak ended. Nikita Kucherov had a three-point showing in a 6-2 win over the Golden Knights to start the trip. He was held off the scoresheet in Denver and ended the night with 1,137 points, tied with former captain Steven Stamkos for tops in Lightning history. Coach Jon Cooper had one word to describe how he understands his complex playmaker. "Experience. Because I've got to experience Kuch," Cooper said. "You treat everyone fairly, don't treat everyone equally. Kuch is somebody that has garnered, you know, you have to let Kuch breathe out there. "Sometimes, people look and think, 'Is he frustrating?' No, you let Kuch be Kuch." After facing Utah on Saturday night, the Lightning will not play again until a home game Thursday against the Winnipeg Jets, who dealt disgruntled goalie Connor Hellebuyck to the New Jersey Devils on Friday. --Field Level Media

item.title: DT Kompany se encuentra estable, pero estará de baja varias semanas: Bayern Munich
item.description: El entrenador del Bayern Munich, Vincent Kompany, permanece hospitalizado y se encuentra estable tras sufrir un desmayo durante el entrenamiento del equipo filial el viernes, pero estará de baja durante varias semanas, dijo el director deportivo del club, Max Eberl.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El entrenador del Bayern Munich, Vincent Kompany, permanece hospitalizado y se encuentra estable tras sufrir un desmayo durante el entrenamiento del equipo filial el viernes, pero estará de baja durante varias semanas, dijo el director deportivo del club, Max Eberl. El entrenador belga, de 40 años, llevaba varios días luchando contra un virus y se había perdido algunas sesiones de entrenamiento. Eberl afirmó el sábado que el Bayern dará prioridad a su recuperación y esperará al diagnóstico antes de hablar de una posible reincorporación. "Primero tenemos que averiguar de qué se trata y luego discutiremos con calma cuál será el tiempo de recuperación", declaró Eberl a periodistas en Múnich. "No estamos hablando de días, sino de semanas. Todos debemos tenerlo claro". El Bayern aplazó el partido de su equipo filial tras el desmayo de Kompany, pero en ningún momento se planteó solicitar un aplazamiento del partido de la Bundesliga del domingo en Friburgo, explicó Eberl. El segundo entrenador, Aaron Danks, que se hará cargo del equipo contra el Friburgo, afirmó que había hablado con Kompany únicamente para interesarse por su estado de salud. "Le expliqué que no íbamos a hablar de fútbol. Solo se trataba de interesarme por su salud y asegurarme de que se encuentra bien", dijo Danks. "Todas las decisiones futbolísticas están en nuestras manos". El Bayern lidera la Bundesliga con 14 unidades en seis partidos, por delante del Borussia Dortmund por diferencia de goles, mientras que el Friburgo, tercero, se encuentra a un punto.

item.title: Infantino se ríe de rumores sobre su dimisión, destaca apoyo internacional a campaña de reelección
item.description: El presidente de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, se tomó a broma las preguntas sobre si había considerado dimitir tras el fracaso de la propuesta sobre el control de los derechos comerciales vinculados al Mundial y destacó el apoyo abrumador de las federaciones miembro de todas las confederaciones.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, se tomó a broma las preguntas sobre si había considerado dimitir tras el fracaso de la propuesta sobre el control de los derechos comerciales vinculados al Mundial y destacó el apoyo abrumador de las federaciones miembro de todas las confederaciones. Tres meses después de enfrentarse a peticiones de dimisión tras abandonar la propuesta que buscaba una inversión privada en una nueva entidad que controlara los derechos comerciales vinculados a las principales competiciones de la FIFA, Forward Enterprise (FFE), Infantino se encuentra ahora en una posición de fuerza. Sus perspectivas de reelección se reforzaron el viernes después de que el máximo responsable del fútbol asiático le respaldara para un cuarto mandato. El presidente de la Confederación Asiática de Fútbol (AFC), el jeque Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, afirmó que Asia estaba unida en torno a Infantino. "Fui elegido por 211 federaciones de todo el mundo. Creo que lo importante es que, en una organización como la FIFA, puede haber opiniones diferentes, puntos de vista distintos", declaró Infantino a la BBC mientras se reía ante una pregunta sobre si había considerado dimitir. "Pero si nos tomamos en serio la democracia, el proceso democrático, la creencia de que todo el mundo tiene el mismo voto y la misma voz en todo el mundo, que el fútbol pertenece a todos, entonces también debemos respetar las opiniones de la inmensa mayoría". "Acabo de regresar de Tokio, donde la Confederación Asiática de Fútbol me ha respaldado plenamente. Estuve en Cabo Verde, donde todos los países africanos me han respaldado. Estoy hablando con todas las federaciones de todo el mundo", remarcó. La AFC se había sumado anteriormente a la UEFA y a la CONCACAF en sus críticas a la propuesta de la FFE. Pero la división en la CONCACAF y el cambio de postura de la AFC han dejado a Europa cada vez más aislada, al tiempo que han puesto de manifiesto la falta de un candidato alternativo viable para la presidencia de la FIFA. Infantino aspira a un cuarto mandato hasta 2031 y los posibles candidatos deben presentar sus candidaturas antes del 18 de noviembre. Se disculpó en una reunión del Consejo de la FIFA celebrada en Zúrich la semana pasada por la forma en que se gestionó la propuesta de la FFE, pero eso no convenció a las federaciones de fútbol europeas, como las de Alemania e Inglaterra. No obstante, el dirigente suizo-italiano de 56 años añadió: "Está bien no estar de acuerdo (...) pero tenemos que ser capaces de seguir adelante. Hay diferentes puntos de vista. No siempre es fácil ponerlos a todos de acuerdo, pero debemos respetar -y yo respeto- todas las opiniones y todos los puntos de vista".

item.title: Kim Jong Un visita China a través de nuevo puente fronterizo: funcionarios de Corea del Sur
item.description: El líder norcoreano Kim Jong Un llegó a China el sábado a través de un puente recién inaugurado, informó un funcionario del Gobierno surcoreano.
item.dc:creator: Joyce Lee
item.content:encoded: El líder norcoreano Kim Jong Un llegó a China el sábado a través de un puente recién inaugurado, informó un funcionario del Gobierno surcoreano. Kim llegó a Dandong a través del nuevo puente sobre el río Yalu, que conecta Corea del Norte y China, indicó el funcionario, quien habló bajo condición de anonimato ya que no estaba autorizado a comentar el asunto públicamente. El primer ministro chino, Li Qiang, se reunió con Kim en la ciudad fronteriza, informó otro funcionario surcoreano que también habló bajo condición de anonimato. La visita se produce un día antes del aniversario de la entrada de China en la Guerra de Corea (1950-1953). Kim regresará a Corea del Norte tras la visita del sábado, informó la agencia de noticias surcoreana Yonhap. Un funcionario surcoreano declaró a Reuters que era poco probable que Kim visitara Pekín antes de las reuniones de alto nivel del Partido Comunista de China que comienzan el lunes. El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de China no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. China y Corea del Norte inauguraron este mes, tras un largo retraso, el nuevo puente sobre el río Yalu, su paso fronterizo terrestre más importante, con el objetivo de reactivar el comercio tras años de relaciones tensas y las interrupciones provocadas por la pandemia. Se espera que el puente facilite el transporte de maquinaria pesada, materias primas y productos energéticos que Corea del Norte necesita para su desarrollo. La inauguración es otra señal del acercamiento entre Pekín y Pyongyang, tras dos cumbres entre sus líderes en los últimos 13 meses. La última visita conocida de Kim a China tuvo lugar en septiembre de 2025, para asistir a las celebraciones del 80º aniversario del Día de la Victoria en Pekín, ocasión en la que mantuvo una cumbre con el presidente chino, Xi Jinping, que por su parte realizó una visita de Estado a Corea del Norte en junio. China, que luchó junto a Corea del Norte en la Guerra de Corea, es el principal respaldo económico y diplomático de Pyongyang y representa la mayor parte de su comercio oficial. Sin embargo, Corea del Norte se ha acercado a Rusia desde que Moscú lanzara su invasión a gran escala de Ucrania en 2022, lo que, según los analistas, ha reducido su dependencia de Pekín.

item.title: Caleb Wilson, Bulls bid to pick up steam vs. Wizards
item.description: Chicago Bulls rookie forward Caleb Wilson overcame a shaky debut this week with a 21-point, six-rebound effort to help key Friday's come-from-behind victory in Milwaukee.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Chicago Bulls rookie forward Caleb Wilson overcame a shaky debut this week with a 21-point, six-rebound effort to help key Friday's come-from-behind victory in Milwaukee. As the Bulls prepare to face the Washington Wizards in Chicago's home opener on Saturday night, Wilson is eager to keep building -- and working. "I mean, I feel like I'm built for the moment, so whenever I get that chance, I'm going to go out there and show what I can do," he said on Friday. "It's a great opportunity, but we play again tomorrow, so I'm already on to the next." After absorbing a 43-point blowout against host Toronto on opening night Wednesday in a game in which Wilson went only 7 of 21 from the field and finished with 16 points, the Bulls recovered from an early double-digit deficit in Milwaukee to prevail 132-125. Offseason addition Norman Powell paced Chicago with 25 points, while Jalen Smith notched a 14-point, 13-rebound double-double. The Bulls received four double-digit scoring efforts from their bench, with Leonard Miller leading the way with 19 points on 7-for-11 shooting from the field. Reserve Noa Essengue had three steals and has shown an early penchant for adapting to first-year coach Tiago Splitter's aggressive defensive style. "He's another player. He just goes hard every possession, wants to guard the best player on the other team, can slide his feet in front of other people," Splitter said. "He's long. His arms create so many deflections. He's been outstanding." Washington has matched Chicago's results in the first two games of the season, albeit in different order. Anthony Davis' dazzling team debut (34 points, 12 rebounds) keyed a 128-116 victory against Milwaukee on Wednesday, but the Wizards couldn't sustain the momentum Friday in a 112-102 home loss to Toronto. While the Wizards whittled a 17-point, second-quarter deficit to one point in the third, they couldn't compensate for the Raptors' staunch defense. After forcing the Bulls into 27 turnovers on Wednesday, Toronto led Washington into committing 23 on Friday night. Trae Young kept the Wizards afloat with a 22-point, 12-assist double-double but also had four turnovers, one of three Washington players with at least that many. Kyshawn George had a team-high eight turnovers for the Wizards. "Playing in crowds a little bit too much," Washington coach Brian Keefe said. "This is kind of what [Toronto] does. This is a good lesson for us. We're going to learn a lot from this game, but he'll bounce back." Davis scored just nine points to go with nine rebounds. Teammate Tre Johnson added 20 points off the bench, including a 4-for-8 showing from long range. Washington's AJ Dybantsa, the first overall pick in the NBA Draft in June, remained sidelined with a left ankle sprain he sustained in the team's final exhibition game. Keefe said before the Toronto game that Dybantsa is "progressing." --Field Level Media

item.title: Mona Lisa off limits as Paris shuts museums over protest fears
item.description: Cultural centers posted warnings about closures, but some people didn't think to check.
item.dc:creator: Sybille de La Hamaide
item.content:encoded: Disappointed tourists poked their heads through the Louvre's locked gates on Saturday, shut off from the Mona Lisa as galleries and museums across Paris closed as a precaution ahead of fresh demonstrations. "When we came, we thought there could be a problem but not that the museum would be closed," Italian social educator Selena Bertoni, 31, said in front of the Musée d'Orsay. On a four-day trip to Paris she had paid €50 ($56) for two tickets to see its Impressionist paintings and other masterpieces. "Bad timing," she said, with a shrug. The closures came one week after nationwide demonstrations over the cost of living and deteriorating public services descended into some of the [USN:L1N46401W TEXT:"worst street violence"] that France has seen in years. The violence and damage prompted the government to impose localised curfews and close many public venues ahead of demonstrations planned on Saturday. TOP TOURIST DESTINATION The shutdown extended across much of the capital's cultural sector, including the Orangerie, Jeu de Paume and Picasso museums, while the entire Tuileries Gardens complex that leads out of the Louvre was sealed off. "This is the third museum we have come to that is closed. They should've warned us," French visitor Heidi Rosar, 21, said. At the Louvre, the locked black iron gates blocked access to the entire site and the garden. "We wanted to at least see the pyramid," 67-year-old Canadian Don Nowschuk said, referring to the museum's landmark glass entrance. On a two-night stay in the City of Light, Nowschuk suggested the local authorities might be overreacting. "There is so much security that you would think it would be enough to secure the museum," he said. "It's a bit weird to see so many cops with guns around Paris. We are used to guns but not like this." The disruption extended to the performing arts sector. The Paris Opera shuttered both the Palais Garnier and the Opéra Bastille, citing safety concerns for staff and audiences. Organisers of the prestigious Art Basel Paris fair also cancelled its weekend programme. The cultural centres posted warnings about the closures on Friday, but some people never thought to check. "How could we have known? We didn't think a museum could be closed. We are a bit naive," 59-year-old French woman Catherine Sebbagh said. ($1 = 0.8927 euros)

item.title: UAE's Ras Al Khaimah shuts all beaches as neighbours grapple with oil spill
item.description: Ras Al Khaimah authorities said on Saturday that all beaches in the emirate would be closed until further notice, a day after an offshore oil leak prompted beach closures in neighbouring Umm Al Quwain and Sharjah.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ras Al Khaimah authorities said on Saturday that all beaches in the emirate would be closed until further notice, a day after an offshore oil leak prompted beach closures in neighbouring Umm Al Quwain and Sharjah. The Public Services Department announced the closures in a statement shared by Ras Al Khaimah Police General Headquarters. No reason was given. The United Arab Emirates [USN:L1N469029 TEXT:"said on Friday"] that efforts were underway to contain oil leaking from a tanker offshore, with its Ministry of Climate Change and Environment conducting an environmental assessment. All beaches and coastal areas around the city of Umm Al Quwain were temporarily closed until technical teams completed their assessments and determined the necessary safety and marine protection measures, the ministry said. The ministry also urged fishermen and other sea users to avoid affected areas and follow official instructions. Authorities in Sharjah temporarily closed Al Hamriyah Beach, on the UAE's northern coast near the border with Umm Al Quwain, as a precaution, the Sharjah Government Media Bureau said. Since the start of the US-Israeli war with Iran , attacks on commercial vessels in Gulf shipping lanes have heightened concerns about maritime security and the conflict's environmental fallout. Ras Al Khaimah, a northern UAE emirate known for its beaches and luxury resorts, is also home to Wynn Resorts' planned casino resort on Al Marjan Island. The Las Vegas-based operator, which won the UAE's first commercial gaming licence in 2024, said in February it expected the resort to open in the first quarter of 2027. Wynn said in March [USN:L4N44122B TEXT:"it had resumed"] construction after a brief pause, even as the Iran war continued to disrupt businesses across the Middle East. Residents reported unusual odours in parts of Sharjah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain, but the UAE's environment ministry said they posed no health risks. The smell remained pungent across Umm Al Quwain on Friday. UAE authorities have not named the tanker involved in the incident or said what caused the spill.

item.title: Ucrania afirma que Starlink ha vuelto a la normalidad tras una semana de restricciones
item.description: Ucrania afirmó el sábado que el sistema de satélites Starlink y su versión militar, Starshield, volvían a funcionar a altas velocidades tras más de una semana de restricciones que habían entorpecido las operaciones militares y agravado las tensiones con Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ucrania afirmó el sábado que el sistema de satélites Starlink y su versión militar, Starshield, volvían a funcionar a altas velocidades tras más de una semana de restricciones que habían entorpecido las operaciones militares y agravado las tensiones con Estados Unidos. Los problemas con los sistemas propiedad de SpaceX, la empresa de Elon Musk, se produjeron después de que el presidente Donald Trump anunciara un acuerdo para comprar gasóleo ruso, al tiempo que presionaba a Kiev para que dejara de atacar las refinerías de petróleo de Moscú. Las autoridades ucranianas afirmaron que las restricciones dificultaron la capacidad del ejército para interceptar drones de ataque rusos y obligaron a cancelar algunas operaciones. "Los sistemas de seguimiento del Ministerio de Defensa de Ucrania registran oficialmente el restablecimiento de las velocidades de funcionamiento de Starlink/Starshield", declararon las autoridades a través de la aplicación Telegram. "La conectividad se mantiene estable a velocidades superiores a los 400 km por hora". El ejército ucraniano no revela las velocidades máximas de funcionamiento de los sistemas, y el Ministerio de Defensa no ha precisado si el servicio se ha restablecido por completo. Mientras estaban vigentes las limitaciones, Ucrania experimentó problemas al intentar operar a velocidades superiores a los 160 km/h. Ucrania no depende de estos sistemas para las operaciones con drones de largo alcance en territorio ruso, pero Starlink es vital para las comunicaciones en primera línea y Starshield se utiliza para operaciones militares en los territorios ocupados. Ni Musk ni Washington han reconocido su responsabilidad en la restricción de Starlink o Starshield en Ucrania. Ambos han declarado públicamente que cualquier decisión de este tipo solo podría haberla tomado la otra parte. Reuters informó que la orden de limitar Starshield procedía del interior de la Casa Blanca. Anteriormente, los gobiernos de Estados Unidos habían pedido en varias ocasiones a SpaceX que activara o desactivara Starlink en distintos países, indicaron las fuentes. Trump declaró el viernes que, si los problemas persistían, "lo solucionaría".

item.title: Around 1,200 Palestinians are displaced in Hebron as Israel begins military operation
item.description: About 1,200 Palestinians were displaced as the military began an operation in the West Bank a day after a Palestinian attack killed two Israeli soldiers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Israeli military forced around 1,200 Palestinians to leave their homes in Hebron in the occupied West Bank, a Palestinian official said on Saturday, a day after a Palestinian attack [USN:L1N4690KO TEXT:"killed two Israeli"] soldiers. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday had said the military would launch a large-scale operation after the soldiers were killed when when two Palestinian gunmen opened fire at a military checkpoint near the city. The Israeli military said the gunmen were shot dead. They also said the operation in the Al-Jaladah and Ein Deir Baha neighbourhoods near the military checkpoint at the entrance of Hebron was to search for militants and weapons. In a statement, it also said the military would carry out demolitions. The Palestinian Authority criticised the operation as a "collective punishment". Yousef Zouhair Al-Jabari, the head of Hebron's municipality, said around 1,300 faced losing their homes in addition to the 1,200 already displaced. He also said the Israeli operations were motivated by parliamentary elections on Tuesday when Netanyahu's right-wing coalition may lose his majority, opinion polls show. "Netanyahu and the radical ministers in his government are trying to win as many votes as possible from the settlers," Al-Jabari said. The non-governmental organisation the Palestinian Prisoners' Club said Israeli forces had arrested around 70 Palestinians on Friday and Saturday. Israeli officials have not commented on any arrests. NETANYAHU'S GOVERNMENT HAS PRESIDED OVER EXPANSION OF SETTLEMENTS Al-Jabari said the military had demolished shops, factories, homes, and roads in Hebron and that the response was disproportionate and unjustified. Residents in Hebron told Reuters that the military expelled many people with no connection to the Palestinian attackers. "We are calling on officials to stand by us because we are not involved in any of this. There are children. We are isolated; we don’t do anything. This is all arbitrary,” said Majdi Nasser, one of those driven from his home. Residents told Reuters they saw Israeli soldiers marking homes with a black X after their Palestinian occupants had been forced to leave. It was not immediately clear what the X mark meant. Netanyahu's government has presided over a rapid [USN:L6N44Y077 TEXT:"expansion"] of settlements, deemed illegal by UN bodies and most countries, though Israel disputes this. Across the West Bank, Israel has blocked the entrances to most Palestinian cities and towns, severely curtailing Palestinians' freedom of movement. Yousef Mur, a resident of the Palestinian town of Yatta, said the closures meant he was unable to reach Jerusalem with his daughter for her cancer treatment. "The situation is bad, and we are suffering. When we tried to cross, they fired stun grenades towards us, and my girl got scared on the way. They fired stun grenades towards people. The situation is very difficult," Mur said.

item.title: Merz calls for unity as he warns of threats facing Germany
item.description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz called for unity in his struggling coalition on Saturday, saying Germany faced growing threats from political extremists and what he described as daily Russian efforts to destabilise the country.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chancellor Friedrich Merz called for unity in his struggling coalition on Saturday, saying Germany faced growing threats from political extremists and what he described as daily Russian efforts to destabilise the country. Speaking at a conference of the Christian Social Union (CSU), the Bavarian sister party of his conservative Christian Democrats (CDU), Merz said Germany faced "extraordinarily serious challenges". "How do we safeguard our freedom and our security in Europe, in the face of growing threats from extremists within and foreign powers from without?" he said, adding that Russia was seeking "to destabilise Germany on a daily basis". Relations between Berlin and Moscow have fallen to their lowest level since the Cold War following Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine but Russia rejects accusations that it is conducting a hybrid campaign against Germany and other European countries. Merz's comments follow weeks of tension with the ruling coalition after heavy regional election defeats in eastern Germany, where the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) came first in two states and the far-left Left Party topped the poll in Berlin. Merz's approval ratings have fallen to record lows, while tensions have surfaced both between the coalition partners and between the CDU and CSU. The two conservative sister parties have a long history of disagreements but have generally managed to overcome them. On Saturday, delegates broke into loud applause when Merz mentioned Ilse Aigner, the CSU politician the party has proposed as successor to German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, who is due to step down next year. The CDU has so far stopped short of endorsing Aigner, and party sources say it has not abandoned hopes of putting forward its own candidate for the largely ceremonial post of head of state. Merz, who entered the conference hall to a Bavarian brass band playing "The Eye of the Tiger", praised CSU ministers in the government and paid tribute to CSU leader Markus Soeder. But he repeated his rejection of calls from some conservatives to seek ways of cooperating with the AfD, which leads national opinion polls, saying any politician who voted with the party "has no place in our Union". He also urged the Social Democrats (SPD) and Greens not to form a coalition in Berlin with the Left Party, which he accused of tolerating antisemitism within its ranks. The [USN:L1N45Z0ZX TEXT:"Left Party"] denies any systemic antisemitism in the party. Merz said rapid reforms to Germany's pension, tax and welfare systems were essential to revive the economy and restore confidence in public institutions.

item.title: Holder Rybakina sets up Fernandez clash in Ningbo final
item.description: Defending Ningbo Open champion Elena Rybakina overcame Russian sixth seed Diana Shnaider 6-3 7-5 in the semi-final on Saturday to reach another title clash and remind rivals of her threat ahead of next month's WTA Finals.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Defending Ningbo Open champion Elena Rybakina overcame Russian sixth seed Diana Shnaider 6-3 7-5 in the semi-final on Saturday to reach another title clash and remind rivals of her threat ahead of next month's WTA Finals. The world number one will face Leylah Fernandez in the final on Sunday after the unseeded Canadian beat Czech Marie Bouzkova by the same 6-3 7-5 scoreline in the earlier semi at the Yinzhou International Tennis Centre in the eastern Chinese city. Australian and US Open champion Rybakina, who arrived for her title defence after a bruising defeat in Beijing and a foot injury that forced her out of Wuhan, showed flashes of her best form despite a few wobbles against the 13th-ranked Shnaider. "She (Shnaider) played really well and it's always difficult to play against left-handers. We don't have so many on the tour," said Rybakina, who faces a similar test against Fernandez. "I needed some time. The returns were not as bad but during the rallies to switch the pattern was a little bit of an issue for me, but I'm happy I managed to win in two sets." An aggressive start with powerful winners from deep helped three-times Grand Slam winner Rybakina take full control of the opening frame, which she sealed on her 11th set point after a sudden dip in form. 'SO MANY OPPORTUNITIES' "It was an important game and it was a long one," added the top-seeded Rybakina. "It was on my serve and it was a struggle ... I was playing the first balls really well but I couldn't close the game ... so many opportunities, but I'm glad it went my way. She played some great shots and great rallies." The 27-year-old continued to struggle with the accuracy of her first serve in the next set, but won the crucial points and carved out a 4-3 advantage with a break, only to be broken to love in the 10th game. Rybakina responded strongly to get her nose in front again in the next game with some big hitting, before closing out the victory with a much more assured display on serve to take her place in the final. She will aim to further sharpen her game in Sunday's final before turning her attention to the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo next week and then launching her WTA Finals title defence at Indian Wells from November 8. "It's never easy," Rybakina said about winning back-to-back trophies at the Ningbo Open. "Of course I'll try to do my best. I'm going to fight and give my all tomorrow."

item.title: Varma leads India fightback in four-wicket victory over New Zealand
item.description: India's middle-order batter Tilak Varma hammered a half-century off 25 balls as India chased down a target of 181 with a ball to spare, taking a 2-0 lead in the five-match Twenty20 series with New Zealand on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India's middle-order batter Tilak Varma hammered a half-century off 25 balls as India chased down a target of 181 with a ball to spare, taking a 2-0 lead in the five-match Twenty20 series with New Zealand on Saturday. New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner's destructive spell (4-21) had left India shaken, with 68 runs needed from the last five overs. But Varma (51) and Nitish Kumar Reddy (26) targeted the pacers in the final three overs to secure a four-wicket win. "The Hyderabadi boys were in play today ... what everyone believed, I have done it, so I'm really proud of myself," said player-of-the-match Varma, who partnered with Reddy to add 69 runs off 30 balls for the seventh wicket. The Christchurch pitch looked slower than in [USN:L1N4680LF TEXT:"Thursday's high-scoring contest "]as India's pacers restricted New Zealand to 43-3 during the powerplay, but Glenn Phillips (70) and Bevon Jacobs (58) turned the innings around, adding 116 for the fourth wicket. Phillips scored his second straight fifty as he hit four boundaries and four sixes before Arshdeep Singh (2-33) got him caught near the fence. Michael Bracewell then scored 10 off two balls to help the hosts reach 180-5. INDIA OVERCOME SHAKY START India's reply got off to a shaky start with Sanju Samson (14) playing out a maiden in the first over before edging Jacob Duffy's slower ball to point. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who replaced the [USN:L4N4690DH TEXT:"injured Ishan Kishan"], scored four before falling to Nathan Smith. Santner's left-arm spin added to the damage, sending back opener Abhishek Sharma (27) before bowling India captain Shreyas Iyer (7) with a flighted ball. Two balls later, Axar Patel nearly cleared the long on boundary but Finn Allen jumped to catch it over his shoulder, tossing it to Daryl Mitchell before he landed over the rope. Naman Dhir, who had helped close out India's chase on Thursday, fought back with a quick 31 off 17 balls, but he too fell to Santner, caught at extra cover to leave India reeling at 112-6 in the 15th over. But Varma, in at number six, hit Duffy for two boundaries before punishing Smith with three fours and a six, getting India within 11 runs of victory with one over left. Varma hit Duffy for four off the second ball of the final over to ease the pressure, before Reddy brought up the winning runs with a shot down mid on. "I feel every individual in our team is a match-winner ... we thought the game was going away from us, but Tilak and Nitish showed immense character," said Iyer. India can seal the series with a win at Wellington on Tuesday.

item.title: Fresh off epic rally, Sixers take on Bucks
item.description: The Philadelphia 76ers' star-studded lineup quickly has proved that no obstacle is too great to overcome.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Philadelphia 76ers' star-studded lineup quickly has proved that no obstacle is too great to overcome. After two come-from-behind wins, including an epic rally in their home opener on Thursday, the Sixers gladly would settle for a more comfortable victory Saturday night when they host the Milwaukee Bucks. Philadelphia opened its season Tuesday with a 106-100 victory in New York, spoiling the Knicks' banner ceremony. The Sixers trailed by 10 points in the second quarter in front of an energized crowd, but they rallied to edge the defending NBA champs. Tyrese Maxey scored 28 points in that game and followed with a 32-point effort in Thursday's wild 114-106 triumph over the Cleveland Cavaliers. The Sixers trailed by as many as 29 points in the first half against the Cavaliers before storming to a victory thanks to key contributions throughout their lineup. In addition to Maxey's productive night, Joel Embiid added 24 points, Jaylen Brown contributed 21, and LeBron James had 17 to go with 10 rebounds. "We all played basketball," Embiid said. "We play at a high level. Everybody had their moment. 'Rese had his moments, JB had his moments, 'Bron had his moments, and I had my moments." For James, who was playing in front of Philadelphia fans for the first time as a Sixer, the experience was not disappointing. "It was everything I dreamed of and more," James said. "Got the boos, that was amazing, and we deserved it, and then we got the cheers. We almost blew the roof off this thing tonight, in a good way. It was a hell of a night." Embiid said he will play in only one of Philadelphia's two games this weekend, although it's not clear which one. The Sixers also could rest James on Saturday, as he appeared on Friday's injury report as questionable due to lower back/sciatica management. In either case, that'll put more pressure on Maxey, who averaged a career-high 28.3 points last season and is at 30 this year. "He's been very impressive," coach Nick Nurse said. "Coming into this year, he seemed to take a level of confidence and maturity jump. He feels so sure of what he can do, which is a big step." Milwaukee, meanwhile, is looking for its first victory after falling to the Washington Wizards and Chicago Bulls this week. The Bucks have given up an average of 130 points per game in the post-Giannis Antetokounmpo era, including 132 in Friday's seven-point loss to the Bulls. "Just defensively, we've got to be a lot better," said Jaime Jaquez, one of the key players the Bucks received when they dealt Antetokounmpo to the Miami Heat in July. "We're actually putting a lot of points on the board, which is a positive for us. But we've just got to understand defensively what it'll take to win." Tyler Herro scored 34 points against Chicago, while Jaquez chipped in with 19 points, 11 rebounds and five assists. Kyle Kuzma notched 14 points and nine boards. "I've got the ultimate confidence in our guys when they step out there," Milwaukee coach Taylor Jenkins said. "... They're beating themselves up, but I just told them to keep their head up. We've just got to keep working on this stuff." --Field Level Media

item.title: Infantino laughs off resignation talk, touts global support as he seeks reelection
item.description: Three months after facing calls to resign after he abandoned the proposal that sought private investment in a new entity controlling commercial rights linked to major FIFA competitions, Infantino now finds himself in a position of strength.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: FIFA president Gianni Infantino laughed off questions about whether he had considered resigning in the wake of the failed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, pointing to overwhelming support from member associations around the globe. Three months after facing calls to resign after he abandoned the proposal that sought private investment in a new entity controlling commercial rights linked to major FIFA competitions, Infantino now finds himself in a position of strength. His prospects for reelection strengthened on Friday after the [USN:L1N46902J TEXT:"head of Asian football endorsed him"] for a fourth term, with Asian Football confederation (AFC) President Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa saying Asia was united behind Infantino. "I was elected by 211 member associations from all over the world. I think what is important is that in an organisation like FIFA, there can be different views, different points of view," Infantino told the BBC as he laughed off a question about whether he had considered stepping down. "But if we are serious about democracy, about the democratic process, about believing that everyone has the same vote and the same voice all over the world, that football belongs to everyone ... then we need to respect as well the views of the vast, vast majority. "I'm just coming back off Tokyo where the Asian Football Confederation has fully endorsed me. I was in Cape Verde where all African countries have endorsed me. I'm speaking to all associations everywhere in the world." The AFC had previously joined European body UEFA and CONCACAF, which represents North and Central America and the Caribbean, in [USN:L6N4470F3 TEXT:"criticising the FFE proposal"]. But a divided CONCACAF and the AFC's U-turn have left [USN:L4N4691GK TEXT:"Europe increasingly isolated"] while exposing the lack of a viable alternative candidate for the FIFA presidency. Infantino is seeking a fourth term until 2031 and potential candidates must submit their nominations by November 18. He apologised at a FIFA Council meeting in Zurich last week over the way the FFE proposal was handled but that did not sway [USN:L8N4611Y3 TEXT:"European football associations"] such as Germany and England. However, the 56-year-old Swiss-Italian administrator added: "It's OK to disagree ... but then we need to be able to move on. "There are different points of view. It's not always easy to bring them all under one roof, but we need to respect and I do respect all opinions all views," Infantino added. "Then it will be up to the FIFA member associations to decide who they want as a president and how they want FIFA to be run."

item.title: Five Italian activists held in West Bank have been repatriated, ministry says
item.description: Five Italian activists who were detained by Israeli forces in the West Bank this week were released and repatriated on Saturday morning, Italy's foreign ministry said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Five Italian activists who were detained by Israeli forces in the West Bank this week were released and repatriated on Saturday morning, Italy's foreign ministry said. [USN:L8N4691RL TEXT:"The women were detained on Thursday"] by Israeli police in Kiryat Arba along with other international activists, while seeking to protect Palestinian farmers during [USN:L8N3W21FE TEXT:"the olive harvest"] in the Israel-occupied territory. Officials from the Italian embassy in Tel Aviv visited them at the airport on Friday evening and said the activists appeared to be in good physical condition. Settlers have intimidated Palestinians [USN:L8N45Y16P TEXT:"harvesting their olives"] in the occupied West Bank for decades, but [USN:L8N4620II TEXT:"violence has increased"] sharply this year, according to Palestinians, activists and the UN. Israeli rights group Yesh Din said it had recorded more than 330 incidents of settler violence linked to this year's olive harvest, which started in late September, including attacks, theft and damage to trees. Israeli security services have said they take [USN:L6N46304S TEXT:"acts of violence"] and criminal activity very seriously. Olives are the backbone of Palestinian agriculture, a sector that accounts for around 8% of GDP and more than 60,000 jobs, according to the Palestinian Authority's agriculture ministry.

item.title: Jordania refuerza la seguridad tras atentado contra una iglesia que deja ocho muertos
item.description: Jordania reforzó la seguridad en centros comerciales, embajadas extranjeras y otros lugares de todo el país, informó el sábado la embajada de Estados Unidos en Amán, mientras las autoridades buscaban a los hombres armados que mataron a ocho personas e hirieron a 40 en un ataque contra una iglesia.
item.dc:creator: Abdelhadi Ramahi
item.content:encoded: Jordania reforzó la seguridad en centros comerciales, embajadas extranjeras y otros lugares de todo el país, informó el sábado la embajada de Estados Unidos en Amán, mientras las autoridades buscaban a los hombres armados que mataron a ocho personas e hirieron a 40 en un ataque contra una iglesia. Los agresores dispararon durante varios minutos a plena luz del día el viernes, durante un funeral celebrado en una iglesia ortodoxa griega de la provincia de Karak, en lo que las autoridades jordanas calificaron de acto de terrorismo extremista. No hubo ninguna reivindicación inmediata de la autoría. Este tipo de atentados son poco frecuentes en Jordania, aunque las autoridades del reino afirman haber frustrado en repetidas ocasiones complots de militantes islamistas en los últimos años. Bahjat al-Rushda, alcalde de la localidad de Shihan, en Karak, se sumó a una larga lista de autoridades que condenaron lo que calificó de ataque "perverso". "Si Dios quiere, este país seguirá siendo seguro", afirmó. Las autoridades indicaron que seguían buscando a los autores del atentado y añadieron que era demasiado pronto para determinar si tenían vínculos con grupos conocidos dentro o fuera de Jordania. "Una masacre en todos los sentidos de la palabra", declaró Tarek Ammarin en un hospital donde se atendía a los heridos. Un familiar de Ammarin resultó herido en el atentado. Las imágenes de video de Reuters mostraban a la policía patrullando el sábado frente a la iglesia de Hamoud, a unos 120 km al suroeste de la capital, Amán. "Esto es consecuencia de una ideología terrorista y de un extremismo ciego, y no permitiremos que la sociedad siga por este camino", declaró el primer ministro Jafar Hassan en una publicación en X. El rey Abdullah de Jordania, aliado de Washington en la lucha contra los grupos islamistas militantes, visitó Karak horas después del atentado y afirmó que los autores serían castigados "con mano de hierro". Los cristianos constituyen una minoría de la población jordana. El país alberga varios lugares bíblicos que atraen a peregrinos cristianos de todo el mundo.

item.title: Bolsonaro y Lula se enfrentan sobre costo de vida y corrupción en último debate electoral de Brasil
item.description: El senador brasileño Flávio Bolsonaro y el presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva se enzarzaron el viernes en una discusión sobre el costo de la vida y se lanzaron ataques personales en el último debate antes de la segunda vuelta del domingo, con ambos tratando de ganarse a los indecisos en una contienda muy reñida.
item.dc:creator: Andre Romani
item.content:encoded: El senador brasileño Flávio Bolsonaro y el presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva se enzarzaron el viernes en una discusión sobre el costo de la vida y se lanzaron ataques personales en el último debate antes de la segunda vuelta del domingo, con ambos tratando de ganarse a los indecisos en una contienda muy reñida. El hijo del expresidente Jair Bolsonaro superó a Lula en la primera vuelta de las elecciones celebrada a principios de este mes, pero las encuestas de opinión han mostrado que ambos están prácticamente empatados. Bolsonaro y Lula reiteraron sus propuestas electorales durante el debate de más de dos horas organizado por Globo, el canal de televisión más visto de Brasil, centrándose en temas como el costo de la vida, el bienestar social y la seguridad, al tiempo que se lanzaban acusaciones mutuas de corrupción. Lula, que aspira a un cuarto mandato tras recuperar la presidencia en 2022, ha defendido los aumentos del salario mínimo por encima de la inflación llevados a cabo por su Gobierno y ha destacado que su administración ayudó a millones de brasileños a salir del hambre. El presidente afirmó que Bolsonaro "es como los estudiantes que se preparan para los exámenes de acceso a la universidad. Pueden memorizar cosas, pero no aprenden". También señaló que "en la urbanización cerrada donde vive Bolsonaro, la gente no pasa hambre". Bolsonaro respondió señalando que los precios de los alimentos para los brasileños subieron durante el mandato de Lula y criticó una reforma fiscal aprobada por el actual Gobierno, pronosticando que las nuevas normas aumentarían la carga fiscal sobre los consumidores. "Lula ni siquiera recuerda la última vez que fue a hacer la compra porque ahora vive en un palacio de lujo". En los primeros segmentos del debate, ambos candidatos limitaron en gran medida la discusión a temas preestablecidos, atenuando los ataques personales que marcaron el único debate anterior de la campaña entre ambos. En un momento, Bolsonaro se disculpó ante Lula tras afirmar que el presidente da a los brasileños con una mano, pero "les quita con nueve dedos". Lula perdió el meñique izquierdo en un accidente mientras trabajaba como tornero en una fábrica. "No voy a aceptar que un ricachón, con una práctica política muy cuestionable, me llame 'nueve dedos'", dijo el presidente, exigiendo una rectificación. "Lula, si te he ofendido llamándote 'nueve dedos', te pido sinceras disculpas", dijo Bolsonaro. Pero añadió: "¿Te disculparás tú ante los brasileños que sufren la inseguridad (...) y están endeudados?". La discusión se caldeó en los últimos minutos del debate, cuando se permitió a los candidatos interactuar sin moderador, mientras Lula y Bolsonaro intentaban vincularse mutuamente al fraude relacionado con la entidad crediticia Banco Master. Lula presionó a Bolsonaro sobre sus supuestos vínculos con el banquero encarcelado Daniel Vorcaro, mientras que el senador interrogó al mandatario sobre las acusaciones que implicaban a su hijo y un fraude en las pensiones. El debate fue uno de los últimos actos de la campaña, ya que la ley electoral brasileña prohíbe a los candidatos emitir anuncios en radio y televisión a partir del sábado. No obstante, pueden celebrar mítines hasta las últimas horas del día.

item.title: Heat, Hornets strive to bounce back after lopsided losses
item.description: The Miami Heat and Charlotte Hornets have something in common -- and they don't like it.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Miami Heat and Charlotte Hornets have something in common -- and they don't like it. Both teams suffered lopsided losses at home on Friday night. Now they'll face off for the first time this season on Saturday night in Charlotte, N.C. The Hornets will try to recover from a 128-81 drubbing by the Atlanta Hawks. "It's one loss on our record," Charlotte guard Sion James said. "Whether we had won or lost, we have to show back up here at 6 o'clock (Saturday) and got to be better. ... Really see what kind of energy and fight we come out with tomorrow, and we expect that to be at a much higher level." Miami fell 128-111 to the Detroit Pistons, and that result was closer than the 25-point setback in the Heat's opener two days earlier vs. Minnesota. Miami gave up 41 first-quarter points against the Timberwolves and 38 in the third quarter to Detroit. The Heat are winless through two games, though newcomer Giannis Antetokounmpo racked up 36 points and 12 rebounds against the Pistons. There are several areas that are concerning, though perhaps not alarming to coach Erik Spoelstra. "We want to establish our mentality," he said. "That's what everybody is trying to do early on." Charlotte allowed 97 points through three quarters to Atlanta and trailed by as many as 49. That created disgruntled Hornets fans during the home opener. "If you hear boos, you've got to be able to play better basketball," Charlotte coach Charles Lee said. Lee said there could be plenty to gain from the experience if the Hornets have the right response. "When things aren't going your way, what is your focus going to be?" he said. "A good learning opportunity for us to realize that there are things that we can control in those moments." Spoelstra said that when opponents go on big runs, errors become more glaring. "How we collectively build a resolve," he said. "That will be something we work on and get better." Charlotte also had troubles on offense, with missed shots and turnovers piling up. "We didn't respond well to it," James said. "A lot of it was good plays defensively. But more often than that, we were just making the wrong decisions with the ball. We were putting ourselves in positions that we didn't need to be in." The Hornets shot 11-for-51 on 3-point attempts. There also are the matters of taking more pride in every possession and valuing the ball, Lee said. "Our biggest thing is less about the volume of what our shot profile looks like," he said, "and more so we want to create the best uncontested shot that we can get." Charlotte swingman Brandon Miller is 4-for-25 on 3-point attempts through two games. "I have the utmost confidence that some of these shots that he's taking he's going to knock down at a higher clip as we just keep going throughout the year," Lee said. --Field Level Media

item.title: Incendio arrasa la antigua casa de huéspedes nazi "Nido del Águila"
item.description: Los bomberos lucharon durante horas para controlar un incendio que arrasó la antigua casa de huéspedes nazi conocida como "El Nido del Águila", en el sur de Alemania, mientras que la policía investigaba la causa tras detener a un hombre cerca del lugar de los hechos, informaron las autoridades el sábado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Los bomberos lucharon durante horas para controlar un incendio que arrasó la antigua casa de huéspedes nazi conocida como "El Nido del Águila", en el sur de Alemania, mientras que la policía investigaba la causa tras detener a un hombre cerca del lugar de los hechos, informaron las autoridades el sábado. Unos 200 bomberos y personal de emergencias de las cercanías de Berchtesgaden, en Baviera, luchaban contra las llamas después de que el edificio, conocido como Kehlsteinhaus, se incendiara el viernes, informó la policía. Construido en 1938 como casa de huéspedes para los funcionarios nazis y sus invitados, el edificio se encuentra en un espectacular entorno alpino sobre Berchtesgaden. Adolf Hitler lo utilizaba ocasionalmente, lo que le valió el apodo de "la casa de té de Hitler". Se encuentra separado de su residencia de verano cercana, el Berghof. El periódico Bild citó a un portavoz de la policía, quien afirmó que el edificio, conservado tras la Segunda Guerra Mundial como monumento histórico vinculado a la época nazi, había sufrido daños tan graves que "probablemente no se podría salvar". La policía había informado anteriormente que había detenido a un hombre cerca del lugar, pero aún no había determinado la causa del incendio. "En estos momentos se está investigando si esta persona está relacionada con el incendio", declaró la policía bávara en un comunicado.

item.title: China's Communist Party names new provincial chiefs ahead of fifth plenum
item.description: China's ruling Communist Party announced key personnel changes in six provinces on Saturday, including two new provincial party chiefs and six officials positioned to become governors, before it holds a closed-door conclave in Beijing from October 26 to 29.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Baptista
item.content:encoded: China's ruling Communist Party announced key personnel changes in six provinces on Saturday, including two new provincial party chiefs and six officials positioned to become governors, before it holds a closed-door conclave in Beijing from October 26 to 29. The official focus of the secretive meeting, also known as a [USN:L1N45D08Z TEXT:"plenum"], in the Chinese capital is expected to be party governance and discipline, though personnel issues could also feature. Here are the appointments: State Council Vice Secretary-General Wang Zhijun was named Communist Party secretary of the southern province of Hunan, replacing Shen Xiaoming Wang is a full member of the Central Committee, the largest of the party's top decision-making bodies Mo Gaoyi, a vice minister at the party's publicity department and director of the State Council Information Office, was named party secretary of the southwestern province of Yunnan, replacing Wang Ning Xie Weijiang, Hunan's deputy party secretary and party chief of Yueyang, a city in the province's northeast, was named secretary of the provincial government's party group, signalling he is set to succeed Governor Mao Weiming Guo Ningning, Fujian's deputy party secretary and party chief of the provincial capital Fuzhou, was named secretary of the provincial government's party group, signalling she is set to become governor Lin Tao was named Fujian deputy party secretary, while Qin Haixiang replaced Guo as Fuzhou party chief Zhuge Yujie, previously deputy party secretary of central Hubei province, was named deputy party secretary of the northwestern province of Qinghai and secretary of its provincial government's party group, signalling he is set to become governor Chen Yongqi, southern Jiangxi's deputy party secretary and head of its political and legal affairs commission, was named secretary of the provincial government's party group, signalling he is set to become governor. His predecessor, Ye Jianchun, was placed under investigation in August for alleged disciplinary violations Zhao Chenxin was named deputy party secretary of the northern province of Hebei and secretary of the provincial government's party group, signalling he is set to succeed Governor Wang Zhengpu Liu Qifan, previously deputy party secretary of Qinghai, was named deputy party secretary of Yunnan and secretary of the provincial government's party group, signalling he is set to succeed Governor Wang Yubo Provincial legislatures must formally elect the gubernatorial appointments, but that is generally a procedural step after the party's decision

item.title: Germany's Merz rejects talk of working with far-right AfD
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz restated his opposition on Saturday to any change in the "firewall" policy of isolating the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) after a number of calls in his party to try to seek ways of working together.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz restated his opposition on Saturday to any change in the "firewall" policy of isolating the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) after a number of calls in his party to try to seek ways of working together. "Anyone who feels they have to vote for these people has no place in our Union. They have no place amongst us," Merz told a meeting of the Christian Social Union (CSU), sister party of his Christian Democrats (CDU).

item.title: La garde à vue du suspect de l'attaque de Trappes prolongée
item.description: La garde à vue du suspect de l'attaque commise vendredi dans les Yvelines, qui a fait un mort et quatre blessés graves, dont une fillette de 12 ans, a été prolongée, a annoncé samedi le parquet national antiterroriste (PNAT).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La garde à vue du suspect de l'attaque commise vendredi dans les Yvelines, qui a fait un mort et quatre blessés graves, dont une fillette de 12 ans, a été prolongée, a annoncé samedi le parquet national antiterroriste (PNAT). Trois membres de son entourage familial et amical ont en outre été placés en garde à vue vendredi soir et dans la nuit, a ajouté le PNAT. L'auteur de l'attaque circulait à bord d'une voiture et a ouvert le feu à l'arme automatique sur des passants. Le PNAT a ouvert une enquête du chef de "tentatives d'assassinats en relation avec une entreprise terroriste, avec la circonstance que les faits ont été commis à raison de l’appartenance vraie ou supposée, à une prétendue race, une ethnie, une nation ou une religion déterminée". Le président de la République Emmanuel Macron, qui s'est rendu vendredi soir à Trappes, l'une des villes où a eu lieu cette attaque, l'a qualifiée d'"attentat terroriste" à "caractère raciste avéré".

item.title: Russia says drone attack damages Togliatti facilities, Ukraine says petrochemical plant hit
item.description: Several industrial facilities were damaged in a drone attack on the Russian city of Togliatti on Saturday, local authorities said, while Ukraine said it had struck a major petrochemical plant there.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Several industrial facilities were damaged in a drone attack on the Russian city of Togliatti on Saturday, local authorities said, while Ukraine said it had struck a major petrochemical plant there. Togliatti mayor Ilya Sukhikh said preliminary reports indicated no fatalities or injuries. He did not specify which facilities had been hit. Ukraine's General Staff said it had struck the Togliattikauchuk petrochemical plant, one of Russia's largest producers of synthetic rubber. The General Staff also reported a strike on the Proton electronics plant in Russia's Oryol region, which Kyiv says manufactures components for cruise and ballistic missiles. Oryol regional governor Andrei Klychkov [USN:L2N46A00F TEXT:"said"] three people were killed on Friday in a Ukrainian missile strike on an unspecified civilian facility in the region. Ukraine's military also reported hitting an aircraft at the Yeysk airfield in southern Russia. Local authorities confirmed an attack in the area but said it caused only minor damage to two apartment buildings. Russia's Defence Ministry said on Saturday that air defences had destroyed 1,297 drones, one French-made SCALP cruise missile and four Ukrainian Neptune missiles over the previous 24 hours.

item.title: MPS investor Norges to oppose Monte dei Paschi's bids to buy Banco BPM and Banca Generali
item.description: Norges Bank Investment Management, Norway's sovereign wealth fund manager, will vote against Monte dei Paschi's proposed bids to buy Banco BPM and Banca Generali , it said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Norges Bank Investment Management, Norway's sovereign wealth fund manager, will vote against Monte dei Paschi's proposed bids to buy Banco BPM (BAMI.MI) and Banca Generali (BGN.MI) , it said on Saturday. The fund manager, which held a 2.98% stake in MPS at the end of December 2025, will also vote against the [USN:L1N4600D0 TEXT:"proposed merger"] of Italian merchant bank Mediobanca (MDBI.MI) into Monte dei Paschi, the sovereign wealth fund said on its website. MPS investors meet on October 29 to vote on CEO Luigi Lovaglio's defence plan against a takeover offer by Intesa Sanpaolo (ISP.MI) Norges will also vote against the proposed distribution of an extraordinary dividend from reserves Its statement said it will instead approve the share buyback programme and the buyout of the shares Mediobanca holds in insurer Generali (GASI.MI) Norges Bank Investment Management said its decisions were based on its voting principles according to which "mergers, acquisitions and other corporate transactions should maximise shareholder returns"

item.title: Bayern boss Kompany stable but sidelined for weeks, says club director
item.description: Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany remains in hospital in a stable condition after collapsing during reserve-team training on Friday but will be sidelined for weeks, the club's sporting director Max Eberl said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bayern Munich manager [USN:L6N469124 TEXT:"Vincent "][USN:L6N469124 TEXT:"Kompany"] remains in hospital in a stable condition after collapsing during reserve-team training on Friday but will be sidelined for weeks, the club's sporting director Max Eberl said on Saturday. The 40-year-old Belgian coach had been battling a virus in recent days and missed some training sessions. Eberl said Bayern would prioritise his recovery and wait for a diagnosis before discussing any potential return. "We need to firstly figure out what it is and then we'll discuss calmly what the recovery time is to be," Eberl told reporters in Munich. "We're not talking about days, but weeks. We all need to be clear on that." Bayern postponed their reserve side's match following Kompany's collapse but never considered seeking a delay to Sunday's Bundesliga trip to Freiburg, Eberl said. "I think the greatest joy for Vinnie would be for us to play well tomorrow and, ideally, get a positive result," he added. "That would probably be one of the best things we could do to help him recover." Assistant coach Aaron Danks will take charge of the team against Freiburg and said he had spoken to Kompany solely to check on his well-being. "I explained to him that we wouldn't be having any football conversations. It was just checking in on his health and making sure he's OK," Danks said. "All the football operations are in our hands and we'll work together as a team to keep the club moving forward." Bayern lead the Bundesliga with 14 points from six matches, ahead of Borussia Dortmund on goal difference, while third-placed Freiburg are one point behind.

item.title: Jordan church attack survivor says assailant pointed handgun at him
item.description: Prayer services had just started at a church in Jordan on Friday when Nasser al-Burqan heard what he thought was an exploding air conditioner. Then the blasts kept coming. He soon realised it was gunfire.
item.dc:creator: Abdelhadi Ramahi
item.content:encoded: Prayer services had just started at a church in Jordan on Friday when Nasser al-Burqan heard what he thought was an exploding air conditioner. Then the blasts kept coming. He soon realised it was gunfire. Some people ran away. He said others, some bleeding, tried to hide in their place of worship where a funeral for his relative had been taking place. Word spread among those gathered that there were fatalities. When the shooting finally stopped after several minutes, Burqan said he got a good look at the assailants behind what Jordanian authorities described as an act of extremist terrorism that [USN:L1N46A01M TEXT:"killed eight people"]. “When everything finally quietened down, I looked out the window behind me and I saw two — one was masked, the other was not, he was carrying a handgun,” said Burqan, a lawyer. He said one of the attackers, standing about 2 meters away, pointed the handgun at him and opened fire. Some shattered glass left blood on his face. He said he told people who wanted to take him for medical treatment he was fine. SON SHOT IN THE LEG A short while later his son, who also attended the mass, called him to say he had been shot in the leg and was being treated in hospital. The attack at the Greek Orthodox Hamoud church in Karak governorate, about 120 km (75 miles) southwest of the capital Amman, shocked the community, part of Jordan’s Christian minority. Such attacks are rare in Jordan, although authorities in the US-allied kingdom say they have repeatedly foiled plots by Islamist militants in recent years. Jordan's King Abdullah, a US partner in the fight against militant Islamist groups, visited Karak hours after the attack and said the perpetrators would be punished "with an iron fist". Authorities have said they are still searching for the attackers, adding it was too early to determine whether they had links to known groups inside or outside Jordan. There has been no immediate claim of responsibility. Security was stepped up at malls, foreign embassies and other locations across Jordan, the US embassy in Amman said on Saturday, as authorities searched for the gunmen who also wounded 40 people.

item.title: With his first smartphone, Lula seeks to catch up to Brazil's online generation
item.description: His choice to finally adopt a foundational artefact of modern life may be a tacit acknowledgment that the 81-year-old president has failed to keep pace with an electorate that spends much of its life online.
item.dc:creator: Luciana Novaes Magalhaes, Oliver Griffin, Lisandra Paraguassu
item.content:encoded: Just days before his 81st birthday, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva this week took ownership of a brand new smartphone, one that former aides said was his first ever. Lula's choice to finally adopt a foundational artefact of modern life may be a tacit acknowledgment that he has failed to keep pace with a Brazilian electorate that now spends much of its life [USN:L1N45Z0NR TEXT:"online"]. That may count against him in Sunday's [USN:L6N45N1A0 TEXT:"presidential runoff"]. "I’m becoming the king of selfies, a real internet user," Lula told supporters at a recent rally in Brasilia, hinting at his renewed efforts to better navigate social media campaigning. Lula’s new technological adventure illustrates a generational shift in Brazilian politics, where a candidate's ability to convert millions of followers across platforms like TikTok, Instagram and WhatsApp into votes can now catapult them to the upper echelons of Brazilian power. During [USN:L1N45L166 TEXT:"congressional elections"] that took place alongside the first round of this month's presidential vote, a number of younger, social media-savvy candidates dominated their races. Running for the right-wing Liberal Party, Nikolas Ferreira, 30, and Lucas Pavanato, 28, both took more than 3 million votes in their respective races, while leftist candidates who were elected with over half a million votes each included Erika Hilton, 33, and Ana Elisa Silva, who is just 21. LULA LEARNS THE ROPES Lula, a former shoeshine boy turned metal worker, trade union leader and global leftist icon, first ran for president in 1989, and is seeking an unprecedented fourth term in office. Standing in his way is right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, who is the [USN:L1N466029 TEXT:"son of ex-President Jair Bolsonaro"] and surprised pollsters by topping the first-round vote. The 45-year-old senator has been engaging voters directly with his own YouTube channel. Ana Elisa Silva, a law student from Minas Gerais, joined Lula's inner circle to help him better navigate the unfamiliar social media landscape after his disappointing first-round performance. "In my view, digital communication is not a generational privilege," Silva told Reuters. "Age may influence familiarity with certain platforms and formats, but it does not determine the ability to communicate, mobilize, or build a community." For a politician like Lula — who freely admits his distaste for cellphones — the change required some adjustments, Silva said. "His political communication trajectory predates the internet. (It was) forged through his relationships with workers, trade unions, grassroots movements, and massive rallies," she said. "This experience remains important, but it needs to align with changes in how people consume information, especially young people." THE EVOLUTION OF POLITICS The emerging power of so-called "influencer politicians" represents the natural evolution of a phenomenon that started with politicians reaching out to social media figures for campaign support, said Maximo Zaldivar, regional director for Latin America and the Caribbean at the International Foundation for Electoral Systems. "The influencer has their own political capital," Zaldivar said, referring to their amassed followings across social media platforms. "That's what they bring to the table and no politician can compete with that." Among "influencer politicians," Ferreira sits in a league of his own. A staunch Bolsonaro supporter and the son of an evangelical pastor, he boasts nearly 25 million followers on Instagram, equivalent to more than 10% of Brazil's population. Though anyone can jump on social media, success demands commitment and consistent messaging, said Julia Zanatta, 41, an influential conservative lawmaker from southern Brazil with over 1 million followers on Instagram. She secured more than half a million votes in this month's election. “I never thought about whether I'd reach more people or if I'd displease anyone,” she said.

item.title: Key dates in the latest slump in US-Ukrainian ties
item.description: After warmer relations between US President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy over the summer, ties have soured in recent weeks, sparking worries of a deeper break between the United States and Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: After warmer relations between US President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy over the summer, ties have soured in recent weeks, sparking worries of a deeper break between the United States and Ukraine. Here is a timeline of the main developments: September 13 Trump calls on Zelenskiy to [USN:L1N45503J TEXT:"stop"] targeting Russian diesel infrastructure. September 21 Trump, in a call, presses Zelenskiy to halt the strikes, the Financial Times reports. October 3 Zelenskiy appears to defy Trump, saying Ukraine will [USN:L1N45P05A TEXT:"double"] down on attacking Russian refineries. October 9 US and Ukrainian officials meet in Miami. Sources tell Reuters that Trump's envoys struck a [USN:L1N4610ZC TEXT:"tough"] tone with Ukraine, saying the US was frustrated with Ukraine's continued strikes on Russian energy targets. Trump says Russia has [USN:L1N45V0MW TEXT:"agreed"] to supply diesel to global markets, and his administration temporarily lifts sanctions on Russian fuel. Zelenskiy calls the move "weak." October 10 Trump says that "it's time for Ukraine to get a [USN:L6N45W06G TEXT:"new"] president" amid continued strikes on refineries. October 11 Trump says Ukraine and Russia have agreed to an "energy [USN:L1N45X021 TEXT:"ceasefire"]" but neither Ukraine nor Russia confirms that they have agreed to it. Mutual strikes continue. October 13 Russia launches two missile strikes in 24 hours without [USN:L1N45Z11U TEXT:"warnings"] from allies, Zelenskiy says. But Trump says the US is still sharing intelligence with Ukraine. October 14 Ukraine says Elon Musk's SpaceX has [USN:L8N4600M6 TEXT:"restricted"] Starlink services, hampering attack and air defense drone missions. October 15 The order to [USN:L1N4610ZC TEXT:"limit"] satellite usage came from inside the White House, Reuters reports. October 16 Ukraine's resumption of strikes on Russian refineries is a "[USN:L1N46203J TEXT:"disgrace"]," Trump says. Zelenskiy welcomes the prospect of a greater role in talks for European allies he calls "[USN:L1N4620UE TEXT:"real"] leaders." Trump says he is [USN:FWN4622VQ TEXT:"waiving"] the application of certain sanctions, restrictions and duties on Russia, citing the US national interest. October 17 Zelenskiy says Trump's move is "[USN:L1N463009 TEXT:"wrong"]." October 19 Trump says Zelenskiy should "get somebody else to [USN:L6N46517L TEXT:"negotiate"]" an end to the war . Zelenskiy says US [USN:L1N4650WT TEXT:"decisions"], including delays in arms shipments and restrictions on intelligence sharing, are "hard to explain." The Kremlin says Russian President Vladimir Putin, Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping could hold a three-way [USN:L1N4650BJ TEXT:"meeting"]. Ukraine says such a gathering could only prolong the war. October 20 Trump calls on Ukraine to [USN:L1N466099 TEXT:"end"] the war and suggests Russia has the upper hand. Zelenskiy says Ukraine is [USN:S8N44Z02V TEXT:"grateful"] that US intelligence and early warnings about Russian ballistic attacks were restored. US envoy Steve Witkoff holds what a US official calls "[USN:L1N466099 TEXT:"constructive"]" talks with Zelenskiy in Norway. October 21 During a visit by Witkoff, Russia [USN:L8N4670TT TEXT:"frees"] Stephen Hubbard, a retired US schoolteacher in custody since 2022. Trump says he had asked Putin for the release. October 22 Russia launches 21 ballistic missiles at Kyiv, authorities report. Zelenskiy says the [USN:S8N461067 TEXT:"attack"] shows Witkoff's talks with Putin had no effect.

item.title: As winter nears, heating oil emerges as hurdle for Republicans in US Senate races
item.description: Democratic candidates have sought to tie the higher costs to Trump's war with Iran.
item.dc:creator: Tim McLaughlin, Nichola Groom, Timothy Gardner, Leah Douglas
item.content:encoded: Eighty-year-old Rick Russman of New Hampshire spent five decades as a Republican. This year, as his state braces for a winter of soaring heating oil costs, he will vote for Democrat Chris Pappas in one of the country's most closely watched Senate races. For Russman, a resident of Kingston, the situation has become so dire that he will rely on a wood stove to help heat his home this winter rather than on heating oil alone. "Fuel that costs more than $6 a gallon is a huge expense," he said.
