item.title: Mumbai Indians promote Pollard to head coach, replacing Jayawardene
item.description: Mumbai Indians have appointed Kieron Pollard as head coach for the 2027 season in place of Mahela Jayawardene, the Indian Premier League team said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Mumbai Indians have appointed Kieron Pollard as head coach for the 2027 season in place of Mahela Jayawardene, the Indian Premier League team said on Saturday. Pollard, who helped the West Indies win the Twenty20 World Cup in 2012 and won five IPL titles with the Mumbai Indians between 2013 and 2020, served as the team's batting coach under Jayawardene before the [USN:L4N46300R TEXT:"Sri Lankan's departure"] last week. Mumbai Indians are the joint most-successful side in IPL history, with five titles, but have struggled since their last victory, finishing outside the playoffs in four of the past six seasons. "Having experienced this journey as a player and then as a coach, I understand what Mumbai Indians stands for and the responsibility that comes with representing the Blue and Gold," the 39-year-old said in a statement. "I look forward to working closely with the players and support staff, building on the team's legacy, helping our talent grow and giving the (fans) many more reasons to celebrate."

item.title: ＧＭＯ、政府に能動的サイバー防御要請 金銭の要求には応じず
item.description:
Kentaro Okasaka
[東京 ２４日 ロイター] - ＧＭＯインターネットは２４日、自社のＦＸ（外国為替証拠...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＧＭＯ、政府に能動的サイバー防御要請　金銭の要求には応じず 14:56 配信

６月５日、千葉県で開催された展示会で撮影（２０２６年　ロイター/Issei Kato）

Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 ２４日 ロイター] - ＧＭＯインターネットは２４日、自社のＦＸ（外国為替証拠金取引）の自動売買サービスが受けたサイバー攻撃について、「能動的サイバー防御」の適用を政府に緊急要請したと発表した。攻撃者とみられる相手から同社に対し金銭の要求があり、応じなければ自社や顧客の情報を公開するとの連絡を受けたという。

要求には応じない方針。警察などと連携して対応するとしている。また、サービスの全利用者に一律５０００円の見舞金を支払うことを決めた。

能動的サイバー防御は、被害が深刻化する前に国や関係機関が主導して攻撃者のインフラや侵入経路を特定し、無力化して被害の未然防止を図る仕組み。同社は今回の事案について、一般国民の取引口座（金融資産）を標的とした不正操作・資産毀損という「極めて悪質かつ前例のない手口」だと判断。政府に先制的な対応を求めることを決めた。

同社によると、今月１９日に顧客からの問い合わせを受け調査を開始。２０日にサービスの一部顧客のサーバー環境への不正なプログラムの設置を確認し、２１日には被害拡大防止のため全プランのサーバーを順次停止した。顧客から取引口座での身に覚えのない操作などの報告があり、２２日に警察へ相談したという。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：金価格が回復傾向、中銀・機関投資家需要が支援 焦点：金価格高騰で溶かされる高級時計、希少なビンテージ品喪失に懸念 アングル：本物はドルか金か、中東混乱で「安全資産」巡る議論再燃 コラム：銀は金より高リターン、産業用需要拡大と供給制約が強気材料に コラム：史上最高値から反落の金、今後も強気材料が相場下支えか 最終更新: 10/24(土) 14:56 ロイター

item.title: Último debate entre Flávio e Lula reedita troca de acusações e avança pouco em propostas
item.description: A dois dias do segundo turno da eleição presidencial, o debate entre os dois candidatos -- o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) -- na TV Globo foi palco de mais um round de trocas de acusações e avançou um pouco em relação à exposição de planos de governo.
item.dc:creator: Maria Marcello
item.content:encoded: A dois dias do segundo turno da eleição presidencial, o debate entre os dois candidatos -- o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) -- na TV Globo foi palco de mais um round de trocas de acusações e avançou um pouco em relação à exposição de planos de governo. Os candidatos foram para o debate com estratégias específicas de olho no eleitor indeciso. Flávio decidiu focar no custo de vida e prometeu manter programas sociais. Lula chamou a atenção para a defesa da democracia e lembrou que foram os governos petistas que criaram e reforçaram os programas sociais em vigor. "Em quatro anos de governo, você consegue comprar mais ou menos com o seu salário?", questionou Flávio. "Está difícil comprar. Quando você consegue comprar, você está levando menos para a sua casa, esse é o legado do atual governo", disse Flávio. Já Lula, não só defendeu a democracia como acusou o adversário de "miliciano". "Eu sou um homem que tenho biografia, tenho história", disse o presidente. "Eu queria, primeiro agradecer... e pedir o voto de vocês no domingo porque ou a gente mantém a democracia funcionando ou a gente vai ter um miliciano governando esse país dentro do Palácio do Planalto", disse Lula, em menção a Flávio que rendeu um direito de resposta ao senador. Flávio negou envolvimento com milícia na sequência -- "isso é coisa da sua cabeça" -- e prometeu classificar as milícias como narcoterroristas. A organização do debate chegou a impor regras sobre a circulação dos candidatos, de forma a evitar desgastes ocorridos no debate de domingo na TV Band. Veículos e entidades paralelamente fizeram o acompanhamento do debate para checagem de fatos. Mas ainda assim, houve uma reedição de trocas de acusações e era perceptível o clima de Fla-Flu na plateia, que em alguns momentos chegou a se manifestar. Lula questionou Flávio sobre posicionamentos públicos do senador contrários a programas sociais e chegou a perguntar ao senador por que se referiu ao Bolsa-Família como "Bolsa-Farelo". Flávio, por sua vez, apontou a gestão petista dos gastos públicos como responsável pelos juros altos, que resvalam no poder de compra da população. No quesito juros, aliás, Lula lembrou que foi no governo de Jair Bolsonaro, pai de Flávio, que foi aprovada a autonomia do Banco Central, entidade responsável pela definição da taxa básica de juros do país. Os candidatos também conseguiram emplacar argumentos e frases com forte apelo, principalmente para os cortes e edições de trechos a serem usados nas redes sociais nessas últimas horas antes da abertura das urnas eleitorais. Em resposta a Flávio, que referiu-se ao presidente como "nove dedos", Lula lembrou que perdeu o dedo em um acidente de trabalho. "Se tem alguém aqui nesse púlpito que sabe o que é o mundo do trabalho sou eu. Se tem alguém que perdeu o dedo com 17 anos fui eu", disse Lula, provocando reações da plateia. "Milhões de trabalhadores se acidentam por irresponsabilidade patronal, que obriga a gente a trabalhar em jornada que a gente tem que trabalhar. Eu era menor e trabalhava à noite, porque ou trabalhava ou não comia e não vou aceitar que um granfino, com uma prática política muito duvidosa, venha me chamar de nove dedos." Após a dura declaração do presidente, Flávio se desculpou, dizendo que não tinha intenção de ser ofensivo. O senador, por outro lado, buscou se apresentar como o candidato da mudança, da novidade. "Nem parece que ele é o atual presidente da República... Ele parece que parou no tempo. Infelizmente o atual presidente da República, as ideias que ele tinha -- que eram boas lá atrás --... hoje não funcionam mais", afirmou. Os dois também cometeram deslizes no decorrer do debate. Lula volta e meia se perdia nas regras e precisava ser lembrado pelo moderador que ainda tinha tempo para desenvolver sua fala. Já Flávio -- questionado por Lula sobre sua escolha em atuar na defesa de um policial acusado de matar uma criança de 5 anos em Niterói, no Rio de Janeiro -- cometeu um equívoco. Na intenção de prestar solidariedade à mãe da menina, que estava na plateia, se confundiu ao chamá-la pelo nome da criança morta. Em outro momento, o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro voltou a ser citado. Lula cobrou Flávio sobre o dinheiro que pediu ao banqueiro -- o senador reafirmou que era para o financiamento de um filme sobre seu pai, o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro. O senador, por sua vez, acusou Lula de receber um uísque do banqueiro de presente. Houve até mesmo uma renovação do desafio de Lula para que os dois abram suas contas bancárias e provem que não são corruptos. Flávio Bolsonaro é alvo de dois inquéritos no STF: um que apura suspeitas relacionadas exatamente ao financiamento do filme "Dark Horse" e outro sobre suspeita de lavagem de dinheiro envolvendo o advogado Willer Tomaz. Mas se Lula não é alvo de investigação criminal conhecida atualmente, Flávio voltou a se concentrar em seu filho, conhecido como Lulinha, que é investigado pela Polícia Federal sobre suposto tráfico de influência. Na segunda metade do debate, quando os ataques e acusações de ambos os candidatos se intensificaram, a plateia começou a se manifestar e a reagir a respostas dos presidenciáveis. O clima, no entanto, foi mais ameno que no debate do último domingo.

item.title: 米司法省、アラスカ上院選の結果認定阻止へ訴訟 「候補者名酷似」理由に
item.description: ［２３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２３日　ロイター］ - 米司法省は２２日、１１月中間選挙のアラスカ州連邦上院選で共和党の現職候補が僅差で敗北した場合に、州による選挙結果の認定を差し止めるよう求める訴訟を起こした。投票用紙にほぼ同姓同名の共和党候補が２人記載されており、有権者の混乱を招く恐れがあると主張している。

アラスカは共和党が上院多数派を維持できるかを左右する可能性のある州の一つで、共和党の現職ダン・Ｓ・サリバン氏が、民主党のメアリー・ペルトラ氏と接戦を繰り広げている。

司法省は、選挙にダン・Ｊ・サリバン・ジュニアという名の共和党候補が出馬していることを問題視。訴状は、同氏が「サリバン上院議員の支持者を誤って自身に投票させる意図を持って」立候補していると主張している。

司法省は訴状で、「有権者の混乱の影響を受けた可能性がある」結果の認定を差し止めるよう要請。これにより「ダニエル・Ｊ・サリバン氏に投じられた票が本来はサリバン上院議員に投じられるはずだったものかどうかを調べる調査」が可能になるとしている。

トランプ大統領は２３日、記者団に対して、訴訟を支持すると述べ「やれと言ったのは私だ」と語った。

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝ＷＳ開幕、ブルワーズが先勝 ミジオロウスキーが最速記録
item.description: ［２３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２３日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）は２３日、ワールドシリーズ（ＷＳ、７回戦制）の第１戦を行い、ブルワーズがレイズを３─２で下し、先勝した。

１９８２年以来４４年ぶりのＷＳ出場となったブルワーズは一回、指名打者クリスチャン・イエリチの適時三塁打で先制し、ウィリアム・コントレラス捕手の適時打で２点目を挙げた。

四回に１点を返されたが、七回にはジャクソン・チョウリオ外野手の適時打で１点を追加。九回には１点差に迫られ、２死二、三塁のピンチを迎えたものの、４番手トレバー・メギル投手が最後の打者を三振に仕留めた。

先発ジェーコブ・ミジオロウスキー投手は５回を投げ、４安打１失点、１四球、３三振で勝利投手となった。試合の初球に時速１０３．５マイル（約１６６．６キロ）を計測し、球速の計測が始まった２００８年以降のＷＳ最速記録を樹立した。

item.title: 北朝鮮の金総書記、「軍事革命」加速を要求 精鋭部隊育成へ
item.description: ［ソウル ２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ソウル　２４日　ロイター］ - 北朝鮮の金正恩朝鮮労働党総書記は、平壌で２日間にわたり開かれた朝鮮人民軍の中隊長会議で、各中隊を自立して戦闘を遂行できる精鋭部隊にするよう求めた。朝鮮中央通信（ＫＣＮＡ）が２４日に伝えた。

今回の会議は、軍事力強化を一貫して政策の優先課題とする金氏の姿勢を鮮明にした。

金氏は１０月２２─２３日に開かれた会議で演説し、「新時代の軍備増強の目標」の達成に向け、全ての中隊が万全の準備を整えるよう求めた。ＫＣＮＡによると、２月の第９回朝鮮労働党大会以降、全軍規模の会議が開かれたのは初めて。

金氏は「最強の軍隊を建設し、われわれの方式による軍事革命を加速させよう」と述べた。

今後５年間の国家の方向性を定める２月の第９回党大会で、金氏は通常戦力の強化を求めるとともに、核兵器とミサイルの開発を進める方針を改めて示していた。

item.title: ＮＢＡ＝八村、古巣レーカーズ戦で16得点 クリッパーズは初黒星
item.description: ［２３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２３日　ロイター］ - 米プロバスケットボール協会（ＮＢＡ）は２３日、各地で試合を行い、八村塁が先発したクリッパーズはレーカーズに１１７─１２５で敗れ、今季初黒星を喫した。

古巣対戦となった八村は計３３分１６秒の出場で、３本の３点シュートを沈めるなど１６得点、６リバウンド、１アシスト、２スチールだった。ダリアス・ガーランドがチーム最多の２６得点を記録した。レーカーズはオースティン・リーブスが２８得点、９アシストで牽引。ルカ・ドンチッチは２３得点、６リバウンド、７アシストも、１１回のターンオーバーを喫した。

セルティックスは昨季王者のニックスに１０７─１０３で競り勝ち、今季初勝利を挙げた。ジェイソン・テイタムが両チーム最多の３６得点に、９リバウンド、７アシストと活躍。ニックスはカールアンソニー・タウンズ、ＯＧ・アヌノビー、マイルズ・マクブライドの３選手が２０得点以上を記録したが及ばなかった。

ロケッツは昨季西地区覇者のスパーズを１１４─１１０で下した。アルペレン・シェングンが両チーム最多の２９得点に、ケビン・デュラントとアメン・トンプソンも２０得点を記録した。スパーズはビクター・ウェンバンヤマが２５得点、１３リバウンドと奮闘した。

ピストンズはヒートに１２８─１１１で勝利し、２連勝とした。ポール・リードが１９得点、１１リバウンド、３アシストのダブルダブルで貢献。ヒートはヤニス・アデトクンボが３６得点、１２リバウンド、５アシストと躍動したが、チーム全体の３点シュート成功率が２９．４％にとどまり、２連敗となった。

ティンバーウルブズはマジックを１１５─９３で下し、２連勝。そのほか、ホークス、ラプターズ、グリズリーズ、トレイルブレイザーズも２連勝とした。

item.title: Atlético de San Luis gana de visita al Atlante en el torneo mexicano de fútbol
item.description: Atlético de San Luis sacó el viernes un triunfo de su visita al Atlante por 1-0 en la decimocuarta jornada del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Atlético de San Luis sacó el viernes un triunfo de su visita al Atlante por 1-0 en la decimocuarta jornada del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano. Con su quinto triunfo, Atlético de San Luis llegó a 19 puntos para ubicarse en el décimo lugar general, cerca de la zona que da acceso a la postemporada. Los clubes que ocupan los primeros ocho lugares de la tabla general al final de las 17 jornadas de la temporada regular clasifican a dicha instancia. En el partido disputado en el estadio Azteca de la Ciudad de México, Atlético de San Luis se puso en ventaja a los 59 minutos por conducto de Benjamín Galdames, quien metió el balón por el ángulo izquierdo con un disparo desde el vértice del área. En el transcurso del encuentro, ambos clubes tuvieron opciones de anotar, pero las atinadas intervenciones de los porteros evitaron que se concretaran. Atlante tuvo la oportunidad más clara de empatar en tiempo de reposición con un tiro penal, pero el portero Gibran Lajud tapó el disparo del paraguayo Walter Clar, quien en el contraremate estrelló el balón en el travesaño a los 94 minutos. En el otro partido que se jugó el viernes, Necaxa y Bravos de Ciudad Juárez empataron 1-1. Para Necaxa anotó Owen González y para Bravos de Ciudad Juárez lo hizo Luca Martínez. El sábado, León jugará ante Toluca, Guadalajara visitará a Monterrey y Pumas UNAM enfrentará a Tigres UANL. El domingo, Atlas será local ante Puebla, el actual campeón Cruz Azul visitará a Querétaro, el líder América jugará ante Pachuca y Tijuana será rival de Santos Laguna.

item.title: Trump foreign policy hits voters in the pocketbook, imperiling Republicans in midterms
item.description: Foreign policy is rarely the deciding factor in US midterm elections. But this time, Trump’s approach to world affairs has itself become a pocketbook issue.
item.dc:creator: Matt Spetalnick
item.content:encoded: Foreign policy is rarely the deciding factor in US midterm elections, when economic considerations usually drive voters’ choices. But this time, with Donald Trump’s war against Iran and his sweeping tariff campaign pushing up costs for Americans, a president’s approach to world affairs has itself become a pocketbook issue. As the November 3 elections approach, there are growing signs that voters are drawing that connection directly, creating a major liability for Trump and his fellow Republicans and imperiling their control of Congress. Those include a Reuters/Ipsos poll earlier this month showing some 78% of Americans [USN:L6N45T0W3 TEXT:"blame Trump's policies"] for rising prices that are outpacing their earnings. Not since 2006, when President George W. Bush’s Republicans lost both legislative chambers while he was mired in the unpopular Iraq war, has a US leader’s handling of international events appeared so central to shaping the midterms outcome. The political backlash for Trump could be even bigger, with opinion polls showing that voters feel the economic pain from high gas prices and rising grocery bills in a way that they didn’t two decades ago. “The bottom line is people are experiencing the impact of Trump’s war and other policies,” said Christopher Preble, a senior fellow at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington. “Now voters have a chance to register their discontent with how he’s dealing with all this.” POLITICS DRIVING FOREIGN POLICY With Trump’s [USN:L6N465159 TEXT:"approval ratings"] touching historic lows, he has left little doubt, despite his public claims to the contrary, that he sees the straight line voters are drawing between his foreign policy and their cost of living. That has prompted some controversial policy moves in the run-up to the elections. Chief among them was Trump’s lifting of sanctions on [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"Russian diesel"] exports aimed at bringing down fuel prices, a step his critics, including some fellow Republicans, say reinforces the impression that he is increasingly siding with Moscow in its war in Ukraine. He has also pressed Kyiv to halt strikes on [USN:L1N46203J TEXT:"Russian refineries"] as he tries to shift the blame for high US gasoline prices despite experts saying the surge in energy costs is mainly the result of the war he launched alongside Israel against Iran nearly eight months ago. At the same time, he has promised not to order any [USN:FWN45U1SW TEXT:"new attack"] on Iran before the midterms, though the US and Israel are widely reported to be preparing for a possible major escalation after the elections. Polls have shown that most voters oppose the war initiated by Trump, who had campaigned on avoiding new foreign interventions. He has insisted Americans should accept temporarily higher gas prices so that he can block Iran from developing a nuclear weapon. Iran says its nuclear program is for civilian purposes. The UN nuclear watchdog and US intelligence community have assessed that Tehran shuttered a nuclear weapons development program in 2003. Some Republican candidates have [USN:L4N45N1R0 TEXT:"distanced themselves"] from Trump on matters ranging from the conflict in the Middle East to the trade war with Canada and his pressure campaign against Ukraine. For its part, Iran has sought to keep oil prices high and hurt Trump in the midterms by deploying new tactics to target ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz and deliberately prolonging the [USN:L8N46515R TEXT:"diplomatic stalemate"], senior Iranian officials have told Reuters. Defending the administration's approach, White House spokesman Matt Middleton said: "President Trump has always been clear about temporary market disruptions as a result of the conflict in Iran, but the contrast between President Trump’s economic record and Democrats’ ruinous alternative is clear." ‘IT’S THE ECONOMY, STUPID’ Midterm elections historically have been seen as a referendum on the performance of the incumbent in the White House. And in one election after another in recent decades, the conventional wisdom has been that economic concerns - “it’s the economy, stupid,” as the Clinton-era adage goes - dominate voters’ choices. Opinion polls for this year’s midterms, including the Reuters/Ipsos survey, show that while voters rank foreign policy low on their list of priorities, it is clear that most Americans see some of Trump’s signature moves on the world stage, such as the Iran war and tariffs, feeding into their higher costs. Other polls have shown that a majority of Americans have also soured more broadly on Trump’s international approach. The Chicago Council on Global Affairs said its latest nationwide survey “finds that most Americans believe the Trump administration’s foreign policy actions have negatively impacted America’s global standing and hurt national and household economic conditions.” Since returning to the White House last year, Trump has shaken up the rules-based global order that Washington helped create from the ashes of World War Two while his relations with allies have steadily worsened and the [USN:L1N45G0ZJ TEXT:"limits of US power"] have been increasingly exposed, analysts say. LEGISLATIVE BALANCE OF POWER IN PLAY Against this backdrop, Democrats are widely projected to [USN:L6N465159 TEXT:"gain control"] of the House of Representatives in the midterms, with the Senate also seen as increasingly in play. For Republicans, losing either chamber could complicate Trump's agenda in the last two years of his second term. But even with a shift in the balance of power on Capitol Hill on November 3, lawmakers will have a hard time reining in Trump’s capacity to pursue foreign policy as he sees fit. Once the ballots are counted, a big question will be whether Trump will feel either restricted or emboldened on the world stage as he enters what is traditionally considered a lame-duck phase - when a president is barred from running again and no longer faces electoral consequences for decisions made. “For many presidents who feel politically constrained (at home), foreign policy is the area where they are able to act with relative freedom,” said Jon Alterman of the Center for Strategic and International Studies think tank in Washington. Analysts say Trump's handling of adversaries such as Iran, Russia, China and even Cuba or his approach to allies across the globe could go either way -- or he could simply lose interest and double down on his string of construction projects, such as the White House ballroom.

item.title: Deni Avdija propels Blazers to comeback victory over Kings
item.description: Deni Avdija scored 26 points and the Portland Trail Blazers overcame a 12-point first-quarter deficit en route to a 128-120 victory over the host Sacramento Kings on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Deni Avdija scored 26 points and the Portland Trail Blazers overcame a 12-point first-quarter deficit en route to a 128-120 victory over the host Sacramento Kings on Friday night. Damian Lillard and Toumani Camara scored 19 points apiece and Sidy Cissoko scored 15 points, all in the first half, as Portland improved to 2-0. Robert Williams III scored 13 points while Ja Morant and Jrue Holiday each had 12 points for the Trail Blazers. Kings rookie Darius Acuff Jr. scored 33 points in his second career game and Domantas Sabonis had 27 points, 19 rebounds and 10 assists for his 69th career triple-double. Zach LaVine scored 22 points, Precious Achiuwa added 14 and Keegan Murray had 12 as Sacramento lost its second straight game to open the season. The contest was the Kings' home opener. Portland shot 47.9% from the field, including 14 of 48 (29.2%) from 3-point range. Camara made five 3-pointers and Donovan Clingan grabbed 10 rebounds for the Trail Blazers. The Kings made 46.2% of their attempts and were 8 of 31 (25.8%) from behind the arc. Portland scored the first 15 points of the third quarter to turn a five-point deficit into a 74-64 advantage. Camara scored the final seven points of the burst. Morant drained a 3-pointer to make it 84-73 just prior to the midway point of the quarter. Sacramento trailed 88-83 after Achiuwa's layup with 3:39 remaining in the period before Portland pushed the lead back to 103-90 on Avdija's floater with 1.3 seconds left. The Trail Blazers had an 8-1 edge in 3-pointers during a 44-point third quarter while committing just one turnover. Lillard's short jumper gave Portland a 113-102 edge with 7:09 remaining. Acuff scored the next six points for Sacramento, and he later connected on a 3-pointer to bring the Kings within 118-113 with 4:51 to play. Sacramento got within three, but Camara responded with a trey to give Portland a 121-115 lead with 3:47 left. Four straight points by Clingan gave the Trail Blazers a seven-point lead with 1:50 to play. Avdija sank two free throws to make it an eight-point margin with 28.3 seconds left as Portland sealed its fifth straight victory over the Kings. Sabonis had 17 points, 12 rebounds and seven assists in the first half, when the Kings never trailed. Sacramento led 64-59 at the break. --Field Level Media

item.title: Uncovering 'heat storms'
item.description: Why we needed new language to describe modern heat waves
item.content:encoded:
Follow on Apple or Spotify . Listen on the Reuters app.

Reuters reporters set out to define a heat wave and uncovered something far bigger: "heat storms" that now blanket vast stretches of the planet. On this episode of On Assignment, the journalists behind the investigation, Maurice Tamman and Ben Welsh, explain how extreme heat became a constant feature of modern life, and why they needed a new language to describe it. Further Reading Giant ‘heat storms’ are scorching the Earth. This is the story of the biggest one on record .

item.title: Lakers ride 39-point 3rd quarter to surge past Clippers
item.description: Austin Reaves scored 28 points and added nine assists while Luka Doncic recorded 23 points as the Los Angeles Lakers used a third-quarter surge to stay perfect through two games with a 125-117 victory over the visiting Los Angeles Clippers on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Austin Reaves scored 28 points and added nine assists while Luka Doncic recorded 23 points as the Los Angeles Lakers used a third-quarter surge to stay perfect through two games with a 125-117 victory over the visiting Los Angeles Clippers on Friday. Walker Kessler scored 22 points, Ziaire Williams contributed 14, while Matisse Thybulle and Quentin Grimes each had 13 as the Lakers won for the ninth time in their past 13 games against the cross-town Clippers. Kessler hit 10 of 14 shots from the floor and is now 22 of 26 over two games with his new team after a trade from the Utah Jazz in July. The Lakers had 13 steals and forced the Clippers into 26 turnovers that they turned into 33 points. Doncic committed 11 turnovers, while Kessler and Grimes led all rebounders with eight apiece. Darius Garland scored 26 points and Brook Lopez added 22 as the Clippers dropped their first road game of the season. Derrick Jones Jr. and Rui Hachimura each scored 16 points. The Clippers shot 49.4% from the floor and 43.2% from 3-point range but lost as the Lakers shot 58.2% from the floor and 43.8% from distance. The Lakers led 77-76 with 7:18 remaining in the third quarter when a 3-pointer from Thybulle kicked off a 14-1 run that gave them a 91-77 lead with 3:43 remaining in the period. The Lakers took a 103-90 lead into the fourth quarter after scoring 39 points in the third while shooting 72.7% from the floor. The Clippers used an 8-0 run to pull within 119-113 on a 3-pointer from Garland with 3:21 to play before Grimes sealed the victory on two free throws with 40.9 seconds remaining for a 125-117 lead. The Clippers led 31-27 after one quarter and went up by as many as 11 points less than three minutes into the second before the Lakers closed the gap. A three-point play by Doncic with 5.6 seconds remaining tied the game 64-64 at the half. Doncic led all scorers with 16 points before the break. --Field Level Media

item.title: Alperen Sengun, Rockets win physical battle against rival Spurs
item.description: Alperen Sengun pounded his way to 29 points, including 14 in the fourth quarter, as the Houston Rockets ground out a 114-110 win over the San Antonio Spurs on Friday in Austin, Texas.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Alperen Sengun pounded his way to 29 points, including 14 in the fourth quarter, as the Houston Rockets ground out a 114-110 win over the San Antonio Spurs on Friday in Austin, Texas. The Rockets led by two at halftime and by four after three quarters. San Antonio rallied to take a 104-103 lead on Dylan Harper's 3-pointer with 4:19 remaining. Houston kept feeding Sengun, who battled inside for a layups, two free throws and a three-point play on three consecutive possessions to put the Rockets ahead 109-104. Harper's emphatic dunk with 46.1 seconds left brought the Spurs within 112-110, and two defensive stops gave San Antonio one final chance with five seconds remaining. The Spurs went to Victor Wembanyama deep in the lane for the tying basket, but Amen Thompson blocked his layup above the rim. Fred VanVleet grabbed the rebound for Houston with 0.6 seconds remaining and sank two free throws to seal the win, the Rockets' second straight to open the season. Kevin Durant and Thompson added 20 points apiece for Houston, with Thompson also collecting 10 rebounds. VanVleet finished with 14 points, and Tari Eason scored 12. Wembanyama paced the Spurs with 25 points and 13 rebounds. Harper had 20 points, De'Aaron Fox added 19 points and nine assists, Stephon Castle tallied 15 points, and Devin Vassell scored 10 for San Antonio, which has opened the season with consecutive losses. Thompson's dunk capped a late Rockets run that gave Houston a 32-27 lead after the first quarter. Houston extended its advantage to 11 points, but the Spurs rallied to tie the game at 56 on Julian Champagnie's 3-pointer with 54.2 seconds left before halftime. The teams then traded baskets before VanVleet sank a 3-pointer at the buzzer to give the Rockets a 61-59 lead at the break. Wembanyama led all scorers and rebounders in the first half with 17 points and seven rebounds. Fox added 10 points. Sengun and Thompson paced Houston with 11 points apiece, while Durant scored 10. The Rockets led by as many as 10 in the third quarter. San Antonio responded with a Champagnie 3-pointer and a pair of free throws from Vassell to pull within four heading into the fourth. --Field Level Media

item.title: ATP roundup: Alexander Bublik survives thriller to reach Almaty semis
item.description: Third-seeded Alexander Bublik of Kazakhstan rallied past fifth-seeded Russian Karen Khachanov 4-6, 7-6 (5), 7-6 (5) in Friday's Almaty Open quarterfinals in Kazakhstan.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Third-seeded Alexander Bublik of Kazakhstan rallied past fifth-seeded Russian Karen Khachanov 4-6, 7-6 (5), 7-6 (5) in Friday's Almaty Open quarterfinals in Kazakhstan. Bublik hammered 21 aces and finished with 49 winners in his first match of the tournament after advancing via a second-round walkover. Khachanov secured the only service break of the match in the opening set, but Bublik responded by winning both ensuing tiebreakers. He will face top-seeded Daniil Medvedev, who reached the semifinals with a 6-4, 6-4 victory over France's Terence Atmane. Medvedev did not face a break point and won 91% of his first-serve points. Seventh-seeded Stefanos Tsitsipas of Greece also advanced in straight sets, defeating Australia's James Duckworth 6-3, 6-4. Tsitsipas fired 15 aces, did not face a break point and won 34 of 37 first-serve points. He will meet qualifier Nikoloz Basilashvili after the Georgian rolled past France's Adrian Mannarino 6-3, 6-1. BNP Paribas Fortis European Open Top-seeded Arthur Fils of France fought off fifth-seeded American Alex Michelsen 6-4, 7-6 (12) to advance to the semifinals in Brussels. Fils needed six match points to finally close out the 14-12 second-set tiebreaker. He won 79% of his first-serve points, recorded six aces and converted three of four break chances in the one-hour, 50-minute match. He will face Germany's Jan-Lennard Struff, who ended Belgium's hopes of a home semifinalist by defeating No. 6 seed Zizou Bergs 6-3, 7-6 (6). The Netherlands' Tallon Griekspoor rallied to eliminate No. 2 Jiri Lehecka of the Czech Republic 4-6, 6-4, 6-3. Griekspoor converted three of four break points and overcame Lehecka's 11 aces to reach his second semifinal of the season. He will play third-seeded Francisco Cerundolo after the Argentine dispatched French qualifier Clement Chidekh 6-2, 6-4. Grand Prix Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes Second-seeded Taylor Fritz topped Germany's Daniel Altmaier 7-6 (5), 6-2 to set up an all-American semifinal at the ATP 250 event in Lyon, France. Fritz beat Altmaier for the first time in three career meetings. He will next face No. 4 seed Tommy Paul, who needed two hours, 45 minutes to subdue France's Corentin Moutet 6-4, 3-6, 6-3. Paul converted five of 10 break point chances and saved 10 of 14 opportunities. Top-seeded Flavio Cobolli of Italy recovered from a set down to defeat fifth-seeded Brandon Nakashima 4-6, 6-4, 6-4. Cobolli will meet countryman Lorenzo Musetti after the No. 6 seed survived another lengthy quarterfinal, edging France's Luca Van Assche 7-6 (5), 6-7 (7), 6-4 in three hours, 33 minutes. --Field Level Media

item.title: ソフトバンクＧ出資のオーペイ、米ＩＰＯで最大44億ドルの評価額目指す
item.description: ［２３日 ロイター］ - ソフトバンクグループが出資するデジタル決済企業オーペイは２３日、米国での新規株式公開（Ｉ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ソフトバンクＧ出資のオーペイ、米ＩＰＯで最大44億ドルの評価額目指す 13:43 配信

［２３日　ロイター］　 - ソフトバンクグループが出資するデジタル決済企業オーペイは２３日、米国での新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）で最大４４億２０００万ドルの評価額を目指すと発表した。新興国で拡大するデジタル金融サービスの需要を取り込む狙い。

ナイジェリアを主力市場とするオーペイは、米国預託株式（ＡＤＳ）約１６００万株を１株当たり１９─２１ドルで売り出し、最大３億６６００万ドルの調達を目指す。

米ＩＰＯ市場は、インフレ率の上昇と人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株の急落で圧力にさらされている。新規上場に対する投資家の意欲が後退し、複数の企業が上場計画の延期を余儀なくされる中でのＩＰＯとなる。

オーペイは２０１８年設立。決済、送金、貯蓄、融資などのデジタル金融サービスを提供し、インドネシア、エジプト、パキスタンでも事業を展開している。

世界で６番目に人口が多いナイジェリアは、アフリカ有数のフィンテック市場に成長。調査会社トラクションによると、モニーポイント、フラッターウェーブ、インタースイッチなどのフィンテック企業を輩出している。

提出書類によると、ソフトバンク系企業は今回の売り出し前の時点でオーペイ株の６．６％を保有している。

item.title: Bolsonaro and Lula clash on living costs, corruption in final Brazil election debate
item.description: Opinion polls have shown the two about even before Sunday's presidential runoff.
item.dc:creator: Andre Romani
item.content:encoded: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva sparred over the cost of living and traded personal attacks on Friday in the last presidential debate before Sunday's runoff, as both candidates sought to win over undecided voters amid a tight race. Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, led Lula in the first round of the election earlier this month, but opinion polls have shown the two candidates [USN:L1N4681FZ TEXT:"about even"] this week after the gap between them narrowed. Bolsonaro and Lula repeated their campaign proposals during the over two-hour debate hosted by Globo, Brazil's most-watched TV channel, focusing on themes such as the cost of living, welfare and security, while exchanging allegations of corruption. Lula, who is seeking his fourth term after winning back the presidency in 2022, has defended his government's above-inflation minimum wage increases and stressed that his administration helped millions of Brazilians to escape hunger. The president said the younger Bolsonaro "is like students studying for college entrance exams. They can memorize things, but they can't learn." He also said that "in the gated community where Bolsonaro lives, people don't go hungry." Bolsonaro responded by saying food prices for Brazilians rose during Lula's administration, and he criticized a tax reform approved by the current government, projecting the new rules would raise the tax burden on consumers. "Lula doesn't even remember the last time he went grocery shopping because he lives in a luxury palace now." The two candidates mostly limited the discussion to pre-established themes in the first few segments of the debate, toning down the [USN:L6N46406G TEXT:"personal attacks"] that marked the only previous debate in the campaign between the two. At one point, Bolsonaro apologized to Lula after saying the president gives to Brazilians with one hand but "takes away with nine fingers." Lula lost his left little finger in an accident while working as a lathe operator in a factory. "I will not accept some rich guy, with a highly questionable political practice, calling me 'nine fingers,'" the incumbent said, demanding a retraction. "Lula, if I offended you by calling you 'nine fingers,' then I sincerely apologize, I sincerely apologize," Bolsonaro said. But he added: "Will you apologize to Brazilians suffering from insecurity ... in debt?" The discussion heated up in the last minutes of the debate, when both candidates were allowed to interact without moderation, as Lula and Bolsonaro sought to link each other to the fraud involving lender Banco Master. Lula pressed Bolsonaro on [USN:L1N4530F5 TEXT:"alleged links"] to the bank's jailed banker Daniel Vorcaro, and Bolsonaro questioned Lula [USN:L1N43X02G TEXT:"about accusations"] involving his son and a pension fraud. The debate was one of the campaign's final events, as Brazilian electoral law bars the candidates from broadcasting radio and TV campaign advertising starting on Saturday. They can still hold rallies until the final hours of the day.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Expands Missile Factory Using Suspected Chinese Technology
item.description: Saudi Arabia appears to be expanding its ballistic missile factory to build larger solid-fuel missiles that could fly farther or carry heavier payloads, according to two U.S. researchers who analyzed more than a year of commercial satellite images. More capable missiles could help Saudi Arabia …
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded:
Saudi Arabia appears to be expanding its ballistic missile factory to build larger solid-fuel missiles that could fly farther or carry heavier payloads, according to two U.S. researchers who analyzed more than a year of commercial satellite images.

More capable missiles could help Saudi Arabia to deter attacks by Iran and make its military more self-reliant, while possibly strengthening its position in a deadly conflict with Yemen’s Tehran-backed Houthi fighters.

But they risk fueling a regional missile race and could deepen opposition in the U.S. Congress to a U.S.-Saudi civilian nuclear agreement that has already raised concerns about proliferation.

Satellite company Planet Labs, based in the U.S., took images of the al-Duwadimi complex about 125 miles (200 km) west of Riyadh between April 2025 and September 2026.

The two researchers, Sam Lair and Michael Duitsman of the Foreign Policy Research Institute, assessed that those images show a new building that houses casting pits — wells in which a mixture of fuel ingredients is poured into missile motor casings and allowed to harden.

The Saudi embassy and Information Ministry did not respond to requests for comment.

The building, flanked by what appear to be walls to protect nearby structures from accidental explosions, is at least twice as large as the one believed to house the plant’s existing casting pits, Lair and Duitsman said in their assessment. The Foreign Policy Research Institute (FPRI) is a non-partisan research organization in Philadelphia.

They said a second new building could store fuel ingredients or finished missile components.

The imagery “suggests that Saudi Arabia is expanding the infrastructure at the missile production complex, likely to produce larger missiles which could deliver larger payloads or reach longer ranges,” they wrote.

Militaries favor solid-fuel missiles because they can be stored for long periods and launched more quickly than liquid-fuel systems.

Lair and Duitsman and experts from the London-based International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) and the CNA research and analysis organization told Reuters that the makeup of Saudi Arabia’s missile force suggests that the al-Duwadimi complex relies on Chinese technology. Lair and Duitsman said that its characteristics also are similar to Chinese missile plants.

Saudi Arabia secretly acquired about 40 liquid-fuel DF-3 ballistic missiles from China in 1987, according to a 1991 declassified CIA estimate. It displayed two of them for the first time in an April 2014 military parade, according to a YouTube video and photographs of the event.

The FPRI team also recently identified from social media videos and photos what they assessed was the wreckage in Yemen of a Saudi-fired Chinese-designed DF-15 missile.

Lair said the kingdom may now be producing the solid-fuel DF-15, and that the expansion of a1-Dumadimi is likely for the production of the longer-range DF-21 or a similar missile.

Riyadh is believed to have turned to Beijing because Washington has long restricted exports of longer-range missile systems.

The Chinese embassy and defense ministry did not respond to requests for comment. The CIA declined to comment. The White House did not respond to a request for comment.

Missiles Would Alter the Balance of Power

Sascha Bruchmann, a research fellow at IISS, said longer-range missiles would allow Saudi Arabia to strike Iran without risking its U.S.-supplied F-15 jet fighters against Iranian air defenses.

“You’d want a system to threaten whatever is holy to Tehran … if you don’t have the political will to send an F-15 with JDAMs over Tehran,” said Bruchmann, referring to U.S.-made satellite-guided bombs. “Iran has a lead because its missiles and drones can strike Saudi wherever it wants. The Saudis could close that capability gap a bit.”

Bruchmann, who reviewed the FPRI analysis at Reuters request, concurred that the expansion of al-Duwadimi could be for producing more powerful solid-fuel missiles.

Janes, the defense intelligence company, also reviewed it and said the buildings “may suggest an effort to expand production capability or support the development of longer-range missiles.”

Saudi Arabia’s apparent pursuit of more powerful missiles comes as other Gulf powers are also seeking to expand their offensive and defensive arsenals, said Decker Eveleth, a CNA analyst who has been tracking the al-Duwadimi construction with commercial satellite imagery and concurred with the FPRI assessment.

“This is being replicated across the Middle East,” he said. “You see exactly the same thing happening in the UAE. You see the exact same thing happening in Turkey. Everybody is doing this now.”

The expansion of al-Duwadimi could have political consequences in the U.S. by stiffening bipartisan congressional opposition to a U.S.-Saudi agreement under which the U.S. would help Riyadh establish uranium enrichment for power generation.

Opponents say that the deal lacks sufficient safeguards to prevent Riyadh from secretly building a nuclear weapon. The kingdom has denied any such plan.

Work Began Last Year

The FPRI assessment said the Planet Labs imagery showed that the expansion at al-Duwadimi began in April 2025 with ground-clearing and digging for the suspected storage building. Work on the suspected casting-pit building began later that month or in early May, it said.

A December 12, 2025, photo showed what researchers assessed were two deep pits inside the building that had no roof yet.

A September 18, 2026, photo shows the roof still partly missing and “heavy-duty blast-diverting walls” on either side to prevent accidental explosions from damaging adjacent structures.

The walls, the researchers said, are somewhat similar to those depicted in imagery of U.S. and Iranian missile plants and “further evidence the building is for casting solid propellant motors.”

Finishing the roofs would not take long, the FPRI said, but installing casting equipment may take several months. The facility could be ready to start producing missiles as early as the end of the year.

item.title: Jaren Jackson Jr., Jazz eke out home-opening win over Pelicans
item.description: Jaren Jackson Jr. logged 24 points and 10 rebounds and Keyonte George added 19 points and 10 assists to rally the Utah Jazz to a 120-119 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Friday in Salt Lake City.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jaren Jackson Jr. logged 24 points and 10 rebounds and Keyonte George added 19 points and 10 assists to rally the Utah Jazz to a 120-119 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Friday in Salt Lake City. Utah rookie Darryn Peterson scored 15 points, including two go-ahead free throws with 50.5 seconds left. Jaxson Hayes chipped in 17 points off the bench and Lauri Markkanen added 16 to help the Jazz beat the Pelicans for the first time since November 2023. New Orleans went 3-0 against Utah each of the previous two seasons and had won eight straight in the series. The Jazz earned the home-opening victory after dropping their overall opener on Wednesday at Memphis. Zion Williamson led the Pelicans with 23 points and reserve Saddiq Bey added 20. Dejounte Murray chipped in 16. Murray missed a potential game-winning jumper with a second left as the Pelicans fell to 0-2. New Orleans center Yves Missi went to the locker room with 6:24 left in the second quarter after sustaining a left knee injury. Missi could not put any weight on his left leg as he was helped off the court. He tallied six points on 3-of-3 shooting in nine minutes. Even without Missi, New Orleans erased a 15-point deficit in the third quarter and took its first lead at 75-74 midway through the quarter on a reverse layup from Murray. The Pelicans scored on 10 consecutive possessions during the rally. Murray accounted for five baskets in that stretch. The Pelicans scored 38 points in the third quarter and carried that momentum into the fourth. Back-to-back baskets from Bennedict Mathurin and Bey helped New Orleans build its largest lead at 99-94. George drained a 3-pointer and fed Hayes for a floater, capping a 15-3 run that put the Jazz back in front 109-102 with 5:35 left. Utah dominated in the paint early to assert control. The Jazz scored 22 of their 31 first-quarter points in the paint. The Jazz never trailed before halftime and claimed a 40-30 lead early in the second quarter behind a 9-0 run. Markkanen and Brice Sensabaugh bookended the surge with 3-pointers. Utah eventually expanded its lead to 67-52 early in the third on another trey from Markkanen. --Field Level Media

item.title: Marquez wins thrilling Australian MotoGP sprint to retake championship lead
item.description: Ducati's Marc Marquez emerged victorious in an electrifying battle with championship rival Jorge Martin before going on to win the Australian Grand Prix sprint from pole position on Saturday and reclaim the MotoGP championship lead.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ducati's Marc Marquez emerged victorious in an electrifying battle with championship rival Jorge Martin before going on to win the Australian Grand Prix sprint from pole position on Saturday and reclaim the MotoGP championship lead. Victory moved seven-times MotoGP champion Marquez up to 365 points in the championship standings, 10 points ahead of Martin, who did not finish the sprint after suffering a gruesome crash in the eighth lap. The reigning champion can further extend that lead in Sunday's race, with Martin declared unfit after breaking his wrist in the crash. After a couple of [USN:L4N4691TI TEXT:"wet qualifying sessions"] earlier in the day, the sprint began on a dry track at the Phillip Island Grand Prix Circuit, with dark clouds looming overhead. Pole-sitter Marquez shot off the line and held on to his lead, though his start was matched by title rival Martin, who barrelled past Alex Marquez and Johann Zarco into second place from fourth. Without the rain to hinder him, Martin squeezed every ounce of pace he could out of his Aprilia on the circuit's swooping corners and stole the lead from Marquez three times, only to overplay his hand and quickly give it away on every occasion. The 2024 champion continued to push, and his overzealousness proved to be his undoing in the eighth lap, as his bike slid out from under him and he went hurtling into the gravel at high speed. "It was a title battle. Of course I gave everything. I was aggressive and he was faster than me, but I tried to defend in the best way possible," Marquez said after his win. "There were nice overtakes, limit overtakes. And in the end, both of us were riding on the limit. Both of us deserved the victory because we are pushing a lot. But, you know, racing is like it is. "Today, it was on my side, but, this (season) is super long, so, keep calm, keep going, and yeah, happy for today." MARTIN TO MISS RACE Martin was carried away from the site of the crash on a stretcher as Aprilia confirmed that he had been taken to the medical centre for evaluation. The Spaniard was later pictured walking out of the medical centre with his arm in a sling and his wrist wrapped up tightly. "Jorge Martin has been declared unfit to race after suffering a fracture to his right wrist! Wishing Jorge a speedy recovery," MotoGP said in a statement on social media. Martin will also be a doubt for next week's Malaysian Grand Prix. Trackhouse Aprilia rider Raul Fernandez, who won the Australian Grand Prix in 2025, was also ruled out of Sunday's race due to inflammation of tissue around a finger fracture that he sustained at the [USN:L1N45X01G TEXT:"Indonesian Grand Prix"] this month. "It’s not how I wanted to say goodbye to Phillip Island, but my finger has said it’s enough. I need to take a break and recover so I can come back at 100%," Fernandez said on social media. Marquez's brother Alex of Gresini Racing finished second, with Fabio Di Giannantonio (VR46 Racing) completing the podium. "It was quite dramatic. For me, I had the best seat, sitting in the third place (behind Marc Marquez and Martin)," Alex said. Martin's teammate Marco Bezzecchi finished in fourth place, keeping his outside shot at winning the title alive. Home hero Jack Miller of Pramac Racing was eighth in the final sprint [USN:L6N46607H TEXT:"at Phillip Island,"] with the Australian Grand Prix moving to the streets of Adelaide next year.

item.title: Moonshot curbs hacking ability in new Kimi model as fears grow over AI-powered cyberattacks
item.description: Moonshot AI has reduced the cyber-offensive capabilities of its newest model, the Chinese startup said on Saturday, as fears grow that increasingly autonomous AI could turbocharge hacking.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Baptista
item.content:encoded: Moonshot AI has reduced the cyber-offensive capabilities of its newest model, the Chinese startup said on Saturday, as fears grow that increasingly autonomous AI could turbocharge hacking. Beijing-based Moonshot announced the curbs while introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro, which it describes as its most capable 3-trillion-parameter-class open-weight model. The company plans to publish the model's weights — files allowing outside developers to run and modify it on their own systems — by November 4. Moonshot said it removed cyber-related data from the training corpus and reinforcement-learning environments used to develop the model, while retaining general coding skills. "We aim not to release open weights that would extend the absolute frontier of cyber capability," the company said. Governments, technology companies and security researchers are growing increasingly concerned that AI could make sophisticated hacking easier and cheaper. Models that can write code, operate software tools and complete long, multi-step tasks may help users identify weaknesses in programs and automate parts of cyberattacks. China [USN:L1N46209C TEXT:"proposed export controls"] last week that would ban exports of AI-driven malware-generation and mutation technology and restrict AI-assisted vulnerability-discovery tools. The draft measures, which remain open for public comment, cite the risk that such capabilities could be used against critical infrastructure, defence-industrial and core government systems, or to bypass security protections. Moonshot said open-weight models can improve security by helping more organisations inspect and secure their own software, including older systems that receive little attention. Unlike proprietary, closed-weight AI systems, however, open-weight releases make central oversight more difficult. Once the files are widely distributed, the original developer has less ability to restrict access, monitor use or update safeguards than with a hosted service. K3.1 Pro scored 81.0% on its internal cyber benchmark, compared with 90.5% for a similar version without the risk-reduction measures, the company said. The test involved finding and exploiting software vulnerabilities in a controlled environment. Moonshot said the comparison showed that filtering cyber-related data reduced the model's offensive cyber performance, although it still outperformed its predecessor. The results have not been independently verified. K3.1 Pro has a 1-million-token context window, allowing it to process very large amounts of text at once. Moonshot also released a faster version, K3.1 Pro Highspeed, which it said runs at two to three times the speed of the standard model.

item.title: Nathan MacKinnon's 4-point night powers Avs past Lightning
item.description: Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and three assists, Mackenzie Blackwood turned away 31 shots, and the Colorado Avalanche beat the Tampa Bay Lightning 6-3 in Denver on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and three assists, Mackenzie Blackwood turned away 31 shots, and the Colorado Avalanche beat the Tampa Bay Lightning 6-3 in Denver on Friday night. Martin Necas had a goal and two assists, Artturi Lehkonen and Devon Toews each collected a goal and an assist, and Nazem Kadri and Fedor Svechkov also scored for Colorado, which snapped a two-game skid. Jake Guentzel scored twice, Charle-Edouard D'Astous added a goal and an assist, Brayden Point had two assists, and Andrei Vasilevskiy made 18 saves for Tampa Bay, which had its three-game winning streak snapped. Toews gave Colorado the early lead when Necas fed him with a cross-ice pass, and he beat Vasilevskiy with a wrist shot 1:08 after the opening faceoff. Kadri made it 2-0 on the power play at 5:52 of the first period, taking a pass from T.J. Hughes in the slot and scoring with a snap shot. The Avalanche extended their lead to 3-0 just 24 seconds into the second period when Svechkov's pass attempt in front of the net deflected off a sprawling Erik Cernak. Svechkov then tapped the puck out of the air and into the net. The Lightning got on the board during one of their five power-play opportunities in the second period when Guentzel scored on a rebound at 8:13. Lehkonen made it 4-1 at 13:57, converting a centering pass from MacKinnon. Tampa Bay answered at the end of another power play when Guentzel stuffed home a pass from Point at 19:17 of the second period. Colorado unsuccessfully challenged the play for a missed stoppage, giving the Lightning another power play. MacKinnon restored Colorado's three-goal lead at 4:18 of the third period. He took a pass from Lehkonen in the neutral zone, skated in on Vasilevskiy and buried a shot inside the near post. D'Astous cut the deficit to 5-3 at 15:13. Vasilevskiy came off for an extra attacker with less than three minutes remaining, and Necas scored into the empty net seconds later. Avalanche forward Logan O'Connor made his season debut, recording three shots in nearly 15 minutes of ice time. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brewers survive harrowing 9th to edge Rays in World Series opener
item.description: MILWAUKEE -- Brewers closer Trevor Megill wasn't perfect, but he was good enough to give Milwaukee a one-game advantage in the World Series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: MILWAUKEE -- Brewers closer Trevor Megill wasn't perfect, but he was good enough to give Milwaukee a one-game advantage in the World Series. Hard-throwing ace Jacob Misiorowski allowed one run over five gritty innings and Megill stranded the tying run at third base to preserve the Brewers' 3-2 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays on Friday night in the opening game of the World Series. Milwaukee, whose only other World Series appearance was a seven-game loss in 1982, scored two runs in the first inning off Nick Martinez and added a run in the seventh on Jackson Chourio's RBI single to go up 3-1. The Rays scored one run in the ninth off Megill, who entered to start the inning and conceded consecutive one-out singles to Jonathan Aranda and Chandler Simpson. Pinch runner Jorge Mateo and Simpson executed a double steal, and Junior Caminero walked to load the bases. Liam Hicks appeared to bounce into a game-ending double play, but a video review showed that shortstop Cooper Pratt was pulled off the bag at second on the throw by second baseman Brice Turang. Hicks was out on the fielder's choice as Mateo scored to make it 3-2, leaving runners on second and third. Megill then struck out Jonny DeLuca for his fifth postseason save in five opportunities. "A lot of times those plays stand during the year, but I'm sure now they have every angle, and they took their time and got it right." Brewers manager Pat Murphy said of the review. "Megill kept his composure. We talk about it all the time. When there's a challenge, do not walk off the mound. Kept his composure, and that was the biggest at-bat of the game." Misiorowski (1-0), whose 1.80 ERA and 252 strikeouts each led the majors during the regular season, allowed one run on four hits in five innings. He fanned three and walked one in a 78-pitch outing. Misiorowski set the tone by throwing a 103.5 mph fastball to open the game, the fastest pitch in World Series history. "I thought Miz was great tonight," Murphy said. "What we're used to seeing in the regular season was Miz just mow through people and have two strikeouts an inning. That's unrealistic. This is the best team in the American League. They proved that during the regular season and proved that in the postseason so far. One of the ways they do that is to make contact better than anybody in baseball." Afterward, the 24-year-old Milwaukee ace was trying to process his first World Series appearance. "I still don't know how I felt. I feel like I'm still trying to take everything in and understand what happened," Misiorowski said. "Obviously went out and did my best and did enough for the team to get a win. That's all I can ask for." After Misiorowski's exit, Abner Uribe and Aaron Ashby combined for three scoreless innings, striking out five. "We came up a little bit short, but there's some benefit maybe from a loss," Rays manager Kevin Cash said. "We saw Ashby. We saw Uribe. We saw Megill. I'd like to think that's going to help us moving forward a little bit." The Brewers posted two quick runs against Martinez (1-1), who got the start when ace Drew Rasmussen was pushed back to Game 2 for an extra day's rest. Chourio singled on the first pitch and scored on Christian Yelich's one-out triple off DeLuca's glove on a diving catch attempt in right-center. William Contreras followed with an RBI single to left. The Rays got a run back in the fourth. Aranda drew a leadoff walk and advanced to third when center fielder Garrett Mitchell misplayed Caminero's 112.7 mph drive into a double. He scored on Hicks' groundout. The Brewers made it 3-1 in the seventh. Steven Matz walked Pratt, who advanced on a groundout and scored on Chourio's two-out single down the right field line against Kevin Kelly. Martinez allowed two runs on five hits in five innings, striking out five and walking none. --Jim Hoehn, Field Level Media

item.title: Taiwan counts 1 dead and 527 injured after Typhoon Champi sweeps past
item.description: Once a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi has weakened but continues to pack wind gusts of around 126 kilometres per hour near its centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

Taiwan counts 1 dead and 527 injured after Typhoon Champi sweeps past

Once a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi has weakened but continues to pack wind gusts of around 126 kilometres per hour near its centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration.

YILAN: Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday (Oct 24), killing 1 person and injuring more than 500, downing trees and severing power, as it continued to weaken and head north towards the Chinese coast though it was not expected to make landfall there. At one point a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi is weakening though still packing gusts of around 126 kilometres per hour (kmh) near its centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration (CWA).

Typhoon Champi swirls over the Philippine Sea, as seen from space on Oct 23, 2026 in this screengrab taken from a handout GIF image. (Photo: Reuters/CSU/CIRA)

The storm was about 150km east of Taiwan, having glanced off the island's northeastern coast in Yilan County early on Saturday, the CWA said. The centre of the storm turned south around midnight, hugging the Yilan coastline before making a rare loop offshore and moving northward away, triggering gusts of about 227kmh in some coastal areas, knocking down power lines and sending roof tiles flying. "MOST TERRIFYING AROUND MIDNIGHT"

"It was most terrifying around midnight," said a retired teacher surnamed Lin as he inspected downed banana trees in his garden in Yilan. "It was a sleepless night. I haven't seen anything like this in many years."

The storm's forecast track shows it turning north, tracking up the Chinese coast and eventually moving into southern Japan. Taiwan's fire department said the death toll remained at one, a man swept away by waves from the island of Liuqiu, with 527 injuries during the heavy wind and torrential rain. Taipower said at one point more than 288,000 homes had lost electricity, though most had been reconnected. The transport ministry said 242 flights were cancelled, an improvement from Friday, when the number was almost 1,000. In the capital Taipei, there were downed trees and on-off squally rain showers.

An uprooted tree after strong winds brought by Typhoon Champi, in Taipei, Taiwan Oct 24, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Ann Wang)

A swathe of northern and central Taiwan, including Taipei, declared a second day of office and school closures on Saturday. Taiwan is generally well prepared for typhoons, which keeps casualties low. Although more common in summer, the storms can strike in autumn too. China's emergency management ministry sent a team to the eastern province of Zhejiang as Champi approached, warning of strong winds and heavy rain through Sunday. It said 400 rescue workers and 600 pieces of equipment had been readied, while more than 41,000 firefighters were on emergency duty. In Taizhou, a city on Zhejiang's coast, more than 3,800 fishing boats returned to harbour, offshore fish-farm workers were brought ashore and 2,084 island visitors were evacuated, state media reported. Authorities halted 25 offshore construction projects and suspended 18 passenger ferry routes.
